texts.jhn.10.9: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and shall find pasture.
texts.jhn.10.10: The thief cometh not, but that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: I came that they may have life, and may have [it] abundantly.
texts.jhn.10.11: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd layeth down his life for the sheep.
texts.jhn.10.12: He that is a hireling, and not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, beholdeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, and the wolf snatcheth them, and scattereth [them]:
texts.jhn.10.13: [he fleeth] because he is a hireling, and careth not for the sheep.
texts.jhn.10.14: I am the good shepherd; and I know mine own, and mine own know me,
texts.jhn.10.15: even as the Father knoweth me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.
texts.jhn.10.16: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice: and they shall become one flock, one shepherd.
texts.jhn.10.17: Therefore doth the Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.
texts.jhn.10.18: No one taketh it away from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment received I from my Father.
texts.jhn.10.19: There arose a division again among the Jews because of these words.
texts.jhn.10.20: And many of them said, He hath a demon, and is mad; why hear ye him?
texts.jhn.10.21: Others said, These are not the sayings of one possessed with a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?
texts.jhn.10.22: And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem:
texts.jhn.10.23: it was winter; and Jesus was walking in the temple in Solomon's porch.
texts.jhn.10.24: The Jews therefore came round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou hold us in suspense? If thou art the Christ, tell us plainly.
texts.jhn.10.25: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believe not: the works that I do in my Father's name, these bear witness of me.
texts.jhn.10.26: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep.
texts.jhn.10.27: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
texts.jhn.10.28: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.
texts.jhn.10.29: My Father, who hath given [them] unto me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch [them] out of the Father's hand.
texts.jhn.10.30: I and the Father are one.
texts.jhn.10.31: The Jews took up stones again to stone him.
texts.jhn.10.32: Jesus answered them, Many good works have I showed you from the Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?
texts.jhn.10.33: The Jews answered him, For a good work we stone thee not, but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.
texts.jhn.10.34: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, ye are gods?
texts.jhn.10.35: If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came (and the scripture cannot be broken),
texts.jhn.10.36: say ye of him, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am [the] Son of God?
texts.jhn.10.37: If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.
texts.jhn.10.38: But if I do them, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know and understand that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.
texts.jhn.10.39: They sought again to take him: and he went forth out of their hand.
texts.jhn.10.40: And he went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was at the first baptizing; and there be abode.
texts.jhn.10.41: And many came unto him; and they said, John indeed did no sign: but all things whatsoever John spake of this man were true.
texts.jhn.10.42: And many believed on him there.
texts.jhn.11.1: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
texts.jhn.11.2: And it was that Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
texts.jhn.11.3: The sisters therefore sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
texts.jhn.11.4: But when Jesus heard it, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified thereby.
texts.jhn.11.5: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
texts.jhn.11.6: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he abode at that time two days in the place where he was.
texts.jhn.11.7: Then after this he saith to the disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.
texts.jhn.11.8: The disciples say unto him, Rabbi, the Jews were but now seeking to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?
texts.jhn.11.9: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.
texts.jhn.11.10: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.
texts.jhn.11.11: These things spake he: and after this he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus is fallen asleep; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
texts.jhn.11.12: The disciples therefore said unto him, Lord, if he is fallen asleep, he will recover.
texts.jhn.11.13: Now Jesus had spoken of his death: but they thought that he spake of taking rest in sleep.
texts.jhn.11.14: Then Jesus therefore said unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.
texts.jhn.11.15: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.
texts.jhn.11.16: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said unto his fellow-disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.
texts.jhn.11.17: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
texts.jhn.11.18: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off;
texts.jhn.11.19: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
texts.jhn.11.20: Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary still sat in the house.
texts.jhn.11.21: Martha therefore said unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
texts.jhn.11.22: And even now I know that, whatsoever thou shalt ask of God, God will give thee.
texts.jhn.11.23: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.
texts.jhn.11.24: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
texts.jhn.11.25: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth on me, though he die, yet shall he live;
texts.jhn.11.26: and whosoever liveth and believeth on me shall never die. Believest thou this?
texts.jhn.11.27: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I have believed that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, [even] he that cometh into the world.
texts.jhn.11.28: And when she had said this, she went away, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is her, and calleth thee.
texts.jhn.11.29: And she, when she heard it, arose quickly, and went unto him.
texts.jhn.11.30: (Now Jesus was not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.)
texts.jhn.11.31: The Jews then who were with her in the house, and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going unto the tomb to weep there.
texts.jhn.11.32: Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, and saw him, fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
texts.jhn.11.33: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews [also] weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,
texts.jhn.11.34: and said, Where have ye laid him? They say unto him, Lord, come and see.
texts.jhn.11.36: The Jews therefore said, Behold how he loved him!
texts.jhn.11.37: But some of them said, Could not this man, who opened the eyes of him that was blind, have caused that this man also should not die?
texts.jhn.11.38: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
texts.jhn.11.39: Jesus saith, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time the body decayeth; for he hath been [dead] four days.
texts.jhn.11.40: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou believedst, thou shouldest see the glory of God?
texts.jhn.11.41: So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou heardest me.
texts.jhn.11.42: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the multitude that standeth around I said it, that they may believe that thou didst send me.
texts.jhn.11.43: And when he had thus spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
texts.jhn.11.44: He that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
texts.jhn.11.45: Many therefore of the Jews, who came to Mary and beheld that which he did, believed on him.
texts.jhn.11.46: But some of them went away to the Pharisees, and told them the things which Jesus had done.
texts.jhn.11.47: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many signs.
texts.jhn.11.48: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.
texts.jhn.11.49: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,
texts.jhn.11.50: nor do ye take account that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.
texts.jhn.11.51: Now this he said not of himself: but, being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for the nation;
texts.jhn.11.52: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God that are scattered abroad.
texts.jhn.11.53: So from that day forth they took counsel that they might put him to death.
texts.jhn.11.54: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed thence into the country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim; and there he tarried with the disciples.
texts.jhn.11.55: Now the passover of the Jews was at hand: and many went up to Jerusalem out of the country before the passover, to purify themselves.
texts.jhn.11.56: They sought therefore for Jesus, and spake one with another, as they stood in the temple, What think ye? That he will not come to the feast?
texts.jhn.11.57: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment, that, if any man knew where he was, he should show it, that they might take him.
texts.jhn.12.1: Jesus therefore six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead.
texts.jhn.12.2: So they made him a supper there: and Martha served; but Lazarus was one of them that sat at meat with him.
texts.jhn.12.3: Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.
texts.jhn.12.4: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, that should betray him, saith,
texts.jhn.12.5: Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred shillings, and given to the poor?
texts.jhn.12.6: Now this he said, not because he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and having the bag took away what was put therein.
texts.jhn.12.7: Jesus therefore said, Suffer her to keep it against the day of my burying.
texts.jhn.12.8: For the poor ye have always with you; but me ye have not always.
texts.jhn.12.9: The common people therefore of the Jews learned that he was there: and they came, not for Jesus' sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.
texts.jhn.12.10: But the chief priests took counsel that they might put Lazarus also to death;
texts.jhn.12.11: because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.
texts.jhn.12.12: On the morrow a great multitude that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
texts.jhn.12.13: took the branches of the palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried out, Hosanna: Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel.
texts.jhn.12.14: And Jesus, having found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,
texts.jhn.12.15: Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass's colt.
texts.jhn.12.16: These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.
texts.jhn.12.17: The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb, and raised him from the dead, bare witness.
texts.jhn.12.18: For this cause also the multitude went and met him, for that they heard that he had done this sign.
texts.jhn.12.19: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Behold how ye prevail nothing: lo, the world is gone after him.
texts.jhn.12.20: Now there were certain Greeks among those that went up to worship at the feast:
texts.jhn.12.21: these therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.
texts.jhn.12.22: Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: Andrew cometh, and Philip, and they tell Jesus.
texts.jhn.12.23: And Jesus answereth them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.
texts.jhn.12.24: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a grain of wheat fall into the earth and die, it abideth by itself alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit.
texts.jhn.12.25: He that loveth his life loseth it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.
texts.jhn.12.26: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will the Father honor.
texts.jhn.12.27: Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause came I unto this hour.
texts.jhn.12.28: Father, glorify thy name. There came therefore a voice out of heaven, [saying], I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.
texts.jhn.12.29: The multitude therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it had thundered: others said, An angel hath spoken to him.
texts.jhn.12.30: Jesus answered and said, This voice hath not come for my sake, but for your sakes.
texts.jhn.12.31: Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
texts.jhn.12.32: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto myself.
texts.jhn.12.33: But this he said, signifying by what manner of death he should die.
texts.jhn.12.34: The multitude therefore answered him, We have heard out of the law that the Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?
texts.jhn.12.35: Jesus therefore said unto them, Yet a little while is the light among you. Walk while ye have the light, that darkness overtake you not: and he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.
texts.jhn.12.36: While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light. These things spake Jesus, and he departed and hid himself from them.
texts.jhn.12.37: But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they believed not on him:
texts.jhn.12.38: that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake, Lord, who hath believed our report? And to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
texts.jhn.12.39: For this cause they could not believe, for that Isaiah said again,
texts.jhn.12.40: He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart; Lest they should see with their eyes, and perceive with their heart, And should turn, And I should heal them.
texts.jhn.12.41: These things said Isaiah, because he saw his glory; and he spake of him.
texts.jhn.12.42: Nevertheless even of the rulers many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess [it], lest they should be put out of the synagogue:
texts.jhn.12.43: for they loved the glory [that is] of men more than the glory [that is] of God.
texts.jhn.12.44: And Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.
texts.jhn.12.45: And he that beholdeth me beholdeth him that sent me.
texts.jhn.12.46: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me may not abide in the darkness.
texts.jhn.12.47: And if any man hear my sayings, and keep them not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
texts.jhn.12.48: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my sayings, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I spake, the same shall judge him in the last day.
texts.jhn.12.49: For I spake not from myself; but the Father that sent me, he hath given me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.
texts.jhn.12.50: And I know that his commandment is life eternal: the things therefore which I speak, even as the Father hath said unto me, so I speak.
texts.jhn.13.1: Now before the feast of the passover, Jesus knowing that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto his Father, having loved his own that were in the world, he loved them unto the end.
texts.jhn.13.2: And during supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's [son], to betray him,
texts.jhn.13.3: [Jesus], knowing that the Father had given all the things into his hands, and that he came forth from God, and goeth unto God,
texts.jhn.13.4: riseth from supper, and layeth aside his garments; and he took a towel, and girded himself.
texts.jhn.13.5: Then he poureth water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.
texts.jhn.13.6: So he cometh to Simon Peter. He saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
texts.jhn.13.7: Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt understand hereafter.
texts.jhn.13.8: Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
texts.jhn.13.9: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.
texts.jhn.13.10: Jesus saith to him, He that is bathed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
texts.jhn.13.11: For he knew him that should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.
texts.jhn.13.12: So when he had washed their feet, and taken his garments, and sat down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?
texts.jhn.13.13: Ye call me, Teacher, and, Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.
texts.jhn.13.14: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, ye also ought to wash one another's feet.
texts.jhn.13.15: For I have given you an example, that ye also should do as I have done to you.
texts.jhn.13.16: Verily, verily, I say unto you, a servant is not greater than his lord; neither one that is sent greater than he that sent him.
texts.jhn.13.17: If ye know these things, blessed are ye if ye do them.
texts.jhn.13.18: I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled: He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me.
texts.jhn.13.19: From henceforth I tell you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am [he].
texts.jhn.13.20: Verily, verily, I say unto you, he that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
texts.jhn.13.21: When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in the spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
texts.jhn.13.22: The disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.
texts.jhn.13.23: There was at the table reclining in Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
texts.jhn.13.24: Simon Peter therefore beckoneth to him, and saith unto him, Tell [us] who it is of whom he speaketh.
texts.jhn.13.25: He leaning back, as he was, on Jesus' breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?
texts.jhn.13.26: Jesus therefore answereth, He it is, for whom I shall dip the sop, and give it him. So when he had dipped the sop, he taketh and giveth it to Judas, [the son] of Simon Iscariot.
texts.jhn.13.27: And after the sop, then entered Satan into him. Jesus therefore saith unto him, What thou doest, do quickly.
texts.jhn.13.28: Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him.
texts.jhn.13.29: For some thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus said unto him, Buy what things we have need of for the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.
texts.jhn.13.30: He then having received the sop went out straightway: and it was night.
texts.jhn.13.31: When therefore he was gone out, Jesus saith, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him;
texts.jhn.13.32: and God shall glorify him in himself, and straightway shall he glorify him.
texts.jhn.13.33: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say unto you.
texts.jhn.13.34: A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another; even as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
texts.jhn.13.35: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
texts.jhn.13.36: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered, Whither I go, thou canst not follow now; but thou shalt follow afterwards.
texts.jhn.13.37: Peter saith unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee even now? I will lay down my life for thee.
texts.jhn.13.38: Jesus answereth, Wilt thou lay down thy life for me? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.
texts.jhn.14.1: Let not your heart be troubled: believe in God, believe also in me.
texts.jhn.14.2: In my Father's house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you; for I go to prepare a place for you.
texts.jhn.14.3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again, and will receive you unto myself; that where I am, [there] ye may be also.
texts.jhn.14.4: And whither I go, ye know the way.
texts.jhn.14.5: Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; how know we the way?
texts.jhn.14.6: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no one cometh unto the Father, but by me.
texts.jhn.14.7: If ye had known me, ye would have known my Father also: from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
texts.jhn.14.8: Philip saith unto him, Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us.
texts.jhn.14.9: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and dost thou not know me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; how sayest thou, Show us the Father?
texts.jhn.14.10: Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I say unto you I speak not from myself: but the Father abiding in me doeth his works.
texts.jhn.14.11: Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works' sake.
texts.jhn.14.12: Verily, verily, I say unto you, he that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater [works] than these shall he do; because I go unto the Father.
texts.jhn.14.13: And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
texts.jhn.14.14: If ye shall ask anything in my name, that will I do.
texts.jhn.14.15: If ye love me, ye will keep my commandments.
texts.jhn.14.16: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may be with you for ever,
texts.jhn.14.17: [even] the Spirit of truth: whom the world cannot receive; for it beholdeth him not, neither knoweth him: ye know him; for he abideth with you, and shall be in you.
texts.jhn.14.18: I will not leave you desolate: I come unto you.
texts.jhn.14.19: Yet a little while, and the world beholdeth me no more; but ye behold me: because I live, ye shall live also.
texts.jhn.14.20: In that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.
texts.jhn.14.21: He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself unto him.
texts.jhn.14.22: Judas (not Iscariot) saith unto him, Lord, what is come to pass that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world?
texts.jhn.14.23: Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my word: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.
texts.jhn.14.24: He that loveth me not keepeth not my words: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father's who sent me.
texts.jhn.14.25: These things have I spoken unto you, while [yet] abiding with you.
texts.jhn.14.26: But the Comforter, [even] the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I said unto you.
texts.jhn.14.27: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
texts.jhn.14.28: Ye heard how I said to you, I go away, and I come unto you. If ye loved me, ye would have rejoiced, because I go unto the Father: for the Father is greater than I.
texts.jhn.14.29: And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe.
texts.jhn.14.30: I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world cometh: and he hath nothing in me;
texts.jhn.14.31: but that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.
texts.jhn.15.1: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
texts.jhn.15.2: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he taketh it away: and every [branch] that beareth fruit, he cleanseth it, that it may bear more fruit.
texts.jhn.15.3: Already ye are clean because of the word which I have spoken unto you.
texts.jhn.15.4: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; so neither can ye, except ye abide in me.
texts.jhn.15.5: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for apart from me ye can do nothing.
texts.jhn.15.6: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
texts.jhn.15.7: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatsoever ye will, and it shall be done unto you.
texts.jhn.15.8: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; and [so] shall ye be my disciples.
texts.jhn.15.9: Even as the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you: abide ye in my love.
texts.jhn.15.10: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
texts.jhn.15.11: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy may be in you, and [that] your joy may be made full.
texts.jhn.15.12: This is my commandment, that ye love one another, even as I have loved you.
texts.jhn.15.13: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
texts.jhn.15.14: Ye are my friends, if ye do the things which I command you.
texts.jhn.15.15: No longer do I call you servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I heard from my Father, I have made known unto you.
texts.jhn.15.16: Ye did not choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that ye should go and bear fruit, and [that] your fruit should abide: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
texts.jhn.15.17: These things I command you, that ye may love one another.
texts.jhn.15.18: If the world hateth you, ye know that it hath hated me before [it hated] you.
texts.jhn.15.19: If ye were of the world, the world would love its own: but because ye are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
texts.jhn.15.20: Remember the word that I said unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.
texts.jhn.15.21: But all these things will they do unto you for my name's sake, because they know not him that sent me.
texts.jhn.15.22: If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin.
texts.jhn.15.23: He that hateth me hateth my Father also.
texts.jhn.15.24: If I had not done among them the works which none other did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.
texts.jhn.15.25: But [this cometh to pass], that the word may be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
texts.jhn.15.26: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, [even] the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall bear witness of me:
texts.jhn.15.27: and ye also bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
texts.jhn.16.1: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be caused to stumble.
texts.jhn.16.2: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you shall think that he offereth service unto God.
texts.jhn.16.3: And these things will they do, because they have not known the Father, nor me.
texts.jhn.16.4: But these things have I spoken unto you, that when their hour is come, ye may remember them, how that I told you. And these things I said not unto you from the beginning, because I was with you.
texts.jhn.16.5: But now I go unto him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
texts.jhn.16.6: But because I have spoken these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.
texts.jhn.16.7: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I go, I will send him unto you.
texts.jhn.16.8: And he, when he is come, will convict the world in respect of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
texts.jhn.16.9: of sin, because they believe not on me;
texts.jhn.16.10: of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye behold me no more;
texts.jhn.16.11: of judgment, because the prince of this world hath been judged.
texts.jhn.16.12: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
texts.jhn.16.13: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he shall guide you into all the truth: for he shall not speak from himself; but what things soever he shall hear, [these] shall he speak: and he shall declare unto you the things that are to come.
texts.jhn.16.14: He shall glorify me: for he shall take of mine, and shall declare [it] unto you.
texts.jhn.16.15: All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he taketh of mine, and shall declare [it] unto you.
texts.jhn.16.16: A little while, and ye behold me no more; and again a little while, and ye shall see me.
texts.jhn.16.17: [Some] of his disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye behold me not; and again a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?
texts.jhn.16.18: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? We know not what he saith.
texts.jhn.16.19: Jesus perceived that they were desirous to ask him, and he said unto them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, A little while, and ye behold me not, and again a little while, and ye shall see me?
texts.jhn.16.20: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
texts.jhn.16.21: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but when she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for the joy that a man is born into the world.
texts.jhn.16.22: And ye therefore now have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one taketh away from you.
texts.jhn.16.23: And in that day ye shall ask me no question. Verily, verily, I say unto you, if ye shall ask anything of the Father, he will give it you in my name.
texts.jhn.16.24: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be made full.
texts.jhn.16.25: These things have I spoken unto you in dark sayings: the hour cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in dark sayings, but shall tell you plainly of the Father.
texts.jhn.16.26: In that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you;
texts.jhn.16.27: for the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came forth from the Father.
texts.jhn.16.28: I came out from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go unto the Father.
texts.jhn.16.29: His disciples say, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no dark saying.
texts.jhn.16.30: Now know we that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.
texts.jhn.16.31: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?
texts.jhn.16.32: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and [yet] I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
texts.jhn.16.33: These things have I spoken unto you, that in me ye may have peace. In the world ye have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
texts.jhn.17.1: These things spake Jesus; and lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that the son may glorify thee:
texts.jhn.17.2: even as thou gavest him authority over all flesh, that to all whom thou hast given him, he should give eternal life.
texts.jhn.17.3: And this is life eternal, that they should know thee the only true God, and him whom thou didst send, [even] Jesus Christ.
texts.jhn.17.4: I glorified thee on the earth, having accomplished the work which thou hast given me to do.
texts.jhn.17.5: And now, Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
texts.jhn.17.6: I manifested thy name unto the men whom thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept thy word.
texts.jhn.17.7: Now they know that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are from thee:
texts.jhn.17.8: for the words which thou gavest me I have given unto them; and they received [them], and knew of a truth that I came forth from thee, and they believed that thou didst send me.
texts.jhn.17.9: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me; for they are thine:
texts.jhn.17.10: and all things that are mine are thine, and thine are mine: and I am glorified in them.
texts.jhn.17.11: And I am no more in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep them in thy name which thou hast given me, that they may be one, even as we [are].
texts.jhn.17.12: While I was with them, I kept them in thy name which thou hast given me: and I guarded them, and not one of them perished, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.
texts.jhn.17.13: But now I come to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
texts.jhn.17.14: I have given them thy word; and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
texts.jhn.17.15: I pray not that thou shouldest take them from the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil [one].
texts.jhn.17.16: They are not of the world even as I am not of the world.
texts.jhn.17.17: Sanctify them in the truth: thy word is truth.
texts.jhn.17.18: As thou didst send me into the world, even so sent I them into the world.
texts.jhn.17.19: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
texts.jhn.17.20: Neither for these only do I pray, but for them also that believe on me through their word;
texts.jhn.17.21: that they may all be one; even as thou, Father, [art] in me, and I in thee, that they also may be in us: that the world may believe that thou didst send me.
texts.jhn.17.22: And the glory which thou hast given me I have given unto them; that they may be one, even as we [are] one;
texts.jhn.17.23: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be perfected into one; that the world may know that thou didst send me, and lovedst them, even as thou lovedst me.
texts.jhn.17.24: Father, I desire that they also whom thou hast given me be with me where I am, that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
texts.jhn.17.25: O righteous Father, the world knew thee not, but I knew thee; and these knew that thou didst send me;
texts.jhn.17.26: and I made known unto them thy name, and will make it known; that the love wherewith thou lovedst me may be in them, and I in them.
texts.jhn.18.1: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where was a garden, into which he entered, himself and his disciples.
texts.jhn.18.2: Now Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus oft-times resorted thither with his disciples.
texts.jhn.18.3: Judas then, having received the band [of soldiers], and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.
texts.jhn.18.4: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were coming upon him, went forth, and saith unto them, Whom seek ye?
texts.jhn.18.5: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am [he]. And Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.
texts.jhn.18.6: When therefore he said unto them, I am [he], they went backward, and fell to the ground.
texts.jhn.18.7: Again therefore he asked them, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.
texts.jhn.18.8: Jesus answered, I told you that I am [he]; if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:
texts.jhn.18.9: that the word might be fulfilled which he spake, Of those whom thou hast given me I lost not one.
texts.jhn.18.10: Simon Peter therefore having a sword drew it, and struck the high priest's servant, and cut off his right ear. Now the servant's name was Malchus.
texts.jhn.18.11: Jesus therefore said unto Peter, Put up the sword into the sheath: the cup which the Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?
texts.jhn.18.12: So the band and the chief captain, and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,
texts.jhn.18.13: and led him to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
texts.jhn.18.14: Now Caiaphas was he that gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
texts.jhn.18.15: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and [so did] another disciple. Now that disciple was known unto the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;
texts.jhn.18.16: but Peter was standing at the door without. So the other disciple, who was known unto the high priest, went out and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
texts.jhn.18.17: The maid therefore that kept the door saith unto Peter, Art thou also [one] of this man's disciples? He saith, I am not.
texts.jhn.18.18: Now the servants and the officers were standing [there], having made a fire of coals; for it was cold; and they were warming themselves: and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.
texts.jhn.18.19: The high priest therefore asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his teaching.
texts.jhn.18.20: Jesus answered him, I have spoken openly to the world; I ever taught in synagogues, and in the temple, where all the Jews come together; and in secret spake I nothing.
texts.jhn.18.21: Why askest thou me? Ask them that have heard [me], what I spake unto them: behold, these know the things which I said.
texts.jhn.18.22: And when he had said this, one of the officers standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?
texts.jhn.18.23: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?
texts.jhn.18.24: Annas therefore sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.
texts.jhn.18.25: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore unto him, Art thou also [one] of his disciples? He denied, and said, I am not.
texts.jhn.18.26: One of the servants of the high priest, being a kinsman of him whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
texts.jhn.18.27: Peter therefore denied again: and straightway the cock crew.
texts.jhn.18.28: They lead Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium: and it was early; and they themselves entered not into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the passover.
texts.jhn.18.29: Pilate therefore went out unto them, and saith, What accusation bring ye against this man?
texts.jhn.18.30: They answered and said unto him, If this man were not an evildoer, we should not have delivered him up unto thee.
texts.jhn.18.31: Pilate therefore said unto them, Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law. The Jews said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:
texts.jhn.18.32: that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should die.
texts.jhn.18.33: Pilate therefore entered again into the Praetorium, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?
texts.jhn.18.34: Jesus answered, Sayest thou this of thyself, or did others tell it thee concerning me?
texts.jhn.18.35: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?
texts.jhn.18.36: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.
texts.jhn.18.37: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end have I been born, and to this end am I come into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.
texts.jhn.18.38: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find no crime in him.
texts.jhn.18.39: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
texts.jhn.18.40: They cried out therefore again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.)
texts.jhn.19.1: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.
texts.jhn.19.2: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and arrayed him in a purple garment;
texts.jhn.19.3: and they came unto him, and said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they struck him with their hands.
texts.jhn.19.4: And Pilate went out again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him out to you, that ye may know that I find no crime in him.
texts.jhn.19.5: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. And [Pilate] saith unto them, Behold, the man!
texts.jhn.19.6: When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify [him], crucify [him]! Pilate saith unto them, Take him yourselves, and crucify him: for I find no crime in him.
texts.jhn.19.7: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by that law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.
texts.jhn.19.8: When Pilate therefore heard this saying, he was the more afraid;
texts.jhn.19.9: and he entered into the Praetorium again, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.
texts.jhn.19.10: Pilate therefore saith unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? Knowest thou not that I have power to release thee, and have power to crucify thee?
texts.jhn.19.11: Jesus answered him, Thou wouldest have no power against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath greater sin.
texts.jhn.19.12: Upon this Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Caesar's friend: every one that maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
texts.jhn.19.13: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out, and sat down on the judgment-seat at a place called The Pavement, but in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
texts.jhn.19.14: Now it was the Preparation of the passover: it was about the sixth hour. And he saith unto the Jews, Behold, your King!
texts.jhn.19.15: They therefore cried out, Away with [him], away with [him], crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.
texts.jhn.19.16: Then therefore he delivered him unto them to be crucified.
texts.jhn.19.17: They took Jesus therefore: and he went out, bearing the cross for himself, unto the place called The place of a skull, which is called in Hebrew, Golgotha:
texts.jhn.19.18: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.
texts.jhn.19.19: And Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. And there was written, JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.jhn.19.20: This title therefore read many of the Jews, for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city; and it was written in Hebrew, [and] in Latin, [and] in Greek.
texts.jhn.19.21: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.
texts.jhn.19.22: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.
texts.jhn.19.23: The soldiers therefore, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.
texts.jhn.19.24: They said therefore one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my garments among them, And upon my vesture did they cast lots.
texts.jhn.19.25: These things therefore the soldiers did. But there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the [wife] of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
texts.jhn.19.26: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!
texts.jhn.19.27: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour the disciple took her unto his own [home].
texts.jhn.19.28: After this Jesus, knowing that all things are now finished, that the scripture might be accomplished, saith, I thirst.
texts.jhn.19.29: There was set there a vessel full of vinegar: so they put a sponge full of the vinegar upon hyssop, and brought it to his mouth.
texts.jhn.19.30: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.
texts.jhn.19.31: The Jews therefore, because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain on the cross upon the sabbath (for the day of that sabbath was a high [day]), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken, and [that] they might be taken away.
texts.jhn.19.32: The soldiers therefore came, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other that was crucified with him:
texts.jhn.19.33: but when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:
texts.jhn.19.34: howbeit one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and straightway there came out blood and water.
texts.jhn.19.35: And he that hath seen hath borne witness, and his witness is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye also may believe.
texts.jhn.19.36: For these things came to pass, that the scripture might be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
texts.jhn.19.37: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.
texts.jhn.19.38: And after these things Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave [him] leave. He came therefore, and took away his body.
texts.jhn.19.39: And there came also Nicodemus, he who at the first came to him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
texts.jhn.19.40: So they took the body of Jesus, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.
texts.jhn.19.41: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new tomb wherein was never man yet laid.
texts.jhn.19.42: There then because of the Jews' Preparation (for the tomb was nigh at hand) they laid Jesus.
texts.jhn.20.1: Now on the first [day] of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, while it was yet dark, unto the tomb, and seeth the stone taken away from the tomb.
texts.jhn.20.2: She runneth therefore, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we know not where they have laid him.
texts.jhn.20.3: Peter therefore went forth, and the other disciple, and they went toward the tomb.
texts.jhn.20.4: And they ran both together: and the other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the tomb;
texts.jhn.20.5: and stooping and looking in, he seeth the linen cloths lying; yet entered he not in.
texts.jhn.20.6: Simon Peter therefore also cometh, following him, and entered into the tomb; and he beholdeth the linen cloths lying,
texts.jhn.20.7: and the napkin, that was upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
texts.jhn.20.8: Then entered in therefore the other disciple also, who came first to the tomb, and he saw, and believed.
texts.jhn.20.9: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
texts.jhn.20.10: So the disciples went away again unto their own home.
texts.jhn.20.11: But Mary was standing without at the tomb weeping: so, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb;
texts.jhn.20.12: and she beholdeth two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
texts.jhn.20.13: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.
texts.jhn.20.14: When she had thus said, she turned herself back, and beholdeth Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.
texts.jhn.20.15: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
texts.jhn.20.16: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turneth herself, and saith unto him in Hebrew, Rabboni; which is to say, Teacher.
texts.jhn.20.17: Jesus saith to her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended unto the Father: but go unto my brethren, and say to them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.
texts.jhn.20.18: Mary Magdalene cometh and telleth the disciples, I have seen the Lord; and [that] he had said these things unto her.
texts.jhn.20.19: When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first [day] of the week, and when the doors were shut where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace [be] unto you.
texts.jhn.20.20: And when he had said this, he showed unto them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord.
texts.jhn.20.21: Jesus therefore said to them again, Peace [be] unto you: as the Father hath sent me, even so send I you.
texts.jhn.20.22: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit:
texts.jhn.20.23: whose soever sins ye forgive, they are forgiven unto them; whose soever [sins] ye retain, they are retained.
texts.jhn.20.24: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
texts.jhn.20.25: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.
texts.jhn.20.26: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them. Jesus cometh, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace [be] unto you.
texts.jhn.20.27: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and see my hands; and reach [hither] thy hand, and put it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
texts.jhn.20.28: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
texts.jhn.20.29: Jesus saith unto him, Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed [are] they that have not seen, and [yet] have believed.
texts.jhn.20.30: Many other signs therefore did Jesus in the presence of the disciples, which are not written in this book:
texts.jhn.20.31: but these are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye may have life in his name.
texts.jhn.21.1: After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested [himself] on this wise.
texts.jhn.21.2: There was together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
texts.jhn.21.3: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also come with thee. They went forth, and entered into the boat; and that night they took nothing.
texts.jhn.21.4: But when day was now breaking, Jesus stood on the beach: yet the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
texts.jhn.21.5: Jesus therefore saith unto them, Children, have ye aught to eat? They answered him, No.
texts.jhn.21.6: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
texts.jhn.21.7: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his coat about him (for he was naked), and cast himself into the sea.
texts.jhn.21.8: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits off), dragging the net [full] of fishes.
texts.jhn.21.9: So when they got out upon the land, they see a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
texts.jhn.21.10: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now taken.
texts.jhn.21.11: Simon Peter therefore went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, the net was not rent.
texts.jhn.21.12: Jesus saith unto them, Come [and] break your fast. And none of the disciples durst inquire of him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
texts.jhn.21.13: Jesus cometh, and taketh the bread, and giveth them, and the fish likewise.
texts.jhn.21.14: This is now the third time that Jesus was manifested to the disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.
texts.jhn.21.15: So when they had broken their fast, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
texts.jhn.21.16: He saith to him again a second time, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Tend my sheep.
texts.jhn.21.17: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, [son] of John, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
texts.jhn.21.18: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
texts.jhn.21.19: Now this he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
texts.jhn.21.20: Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; who also leaned back on his breast at the supper, and said, Lord, who is he that betrayeth thee?
texts.jhn.21.21: Peter therefore seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
texts.jhn.21.22: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee? Follow thou me.
texts.jhn.21.23: This saying therefore went forth among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, that he should not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what [is that] to thee?
texts.jhn.21.24: This is the disciple that beareth witness of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his witness is true.
texts.jhn.21.25: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself would not contain the books that should be written.

texts.jhn.1.1: Au commencement était la Parole, et la Parole était avec Dieu, et la Parole était Dieu.
texts.jhn.1.2: Elle était au commencement avec Dieu.
texts.jhn.1.3: Toutes choses ont été faites par elle, et rien de ce qui a été fait n'a été fait sans elle.
texts.jhn.1.4: En elle était la vie, et la vie était la lumière des hommes.
texts.jhn.1.5: La lumière luit dans les ténèbres, et les ténèbres ne l'ont point reçue.
texts.jhn.1.6: Il y eut un homme envoyé de Dieu: son nom était Jean.
texts.jhn.1.7: Il vint pour servir de témoin, pour rendre témoignage à la lumière, afin que tous crussent par lui.
texts.jhn.1.8: Il n'était pas la lumière, mais il parut pour rendre témoignage à la lumière.
texts.jhn.1.9: Cette lumière était la véritable lumière, qui, en venant dans le monde, éclaire tout homme.
texts.jhn.1.10: Elle était dans le monde, et le monde a été fait par elle, et le monde ne l'a point connue.
texts.jhn.1.11: Elle est venue chez les siens, et les siens ne l'ont point reçue.
texts.jhn.1.12: Mais à tous ceux qui l'ont reçue, à ceux qui croient en son nom, elle a donné le pouvoir de devenir enfants de Dieu,
texts.jhn.1.13: lesquels sont nés, non du sang, ni de la volonté de la chair, ni de la volonté de l'homme, mais de Dieu.
texts.jhn.1.14: Et la parole a été faite chair, et elle a habité parmi nous, pleine de grâce et de vérité; et nous avons contemplé sa gloire, une gloire comme la gloire du Fils unique venu du Père.
texts.jhn.1.15: Jean lui a rendu témoignage, et s'est écrié: C'est celui dont j'ai dit: Celui qui vient après moi m'a précédé, car il était avant moi.
texts.jhn.1.16: Et nous avons tous reçu de sa plénitude, et grâce pour grâce;
texts.jhn.1.17: car la loi a été donnée par Moïse, la grâce et la vérité sont venues par Jésus-Christ.
texts.jhn.1.18: Personne n'a jamais vu Dieu; le Fils unique, qui est dans le sein du Père, est celui qui l'a fait connaître.
texts.jhn.1.19: Voici le témoignage de Jean, lorsque les Juifs envoyèrent de Jérusalem des sacrificateurs et des Lévites, pour lui demander: Toi, qui es-tu?
texts.jhn.1.20: Il déclara, et ne le nia point, il déclara qu'il n'était pas le Christ.
texts.jhn.1.21: Et ils lui demandèrent: Quoi donc? es-tu Elie? Et il dit: Je ne le suis point. Es-tu le prophète? Et il répondit: Non.
texts.jhn.1.22: Ils lui dirent alors: Qui es-tu? afin que nous donnions une réponse à ceux qui nous ont envoyés. Que dis-tu de toi-même?
texts.jhn.1.23: Moi, dit-il, je suis la voix de celui qui crie dans le désert: Aplanissez le chemin du Seigneur, comme a dit Esaïe, le prophète.
texts.jhn.1.24: Ceux qui avaient été envoyés étaient des pharisiens.
texts.jhn.1.25: Ils lui firent encore cette question: Pourquoi donc baptises-tu, si tu n'es pas le Christ, ni Elie, ni le prophète?
texts.jhn.1.26: Jean leur répondit: Moi, je baptise d'eau, mais au milieu de vous il y a quelqu'un que vous ne connaissez pas,
texts.jhn.1.27: qui vient après moi; je ne suis pas digne de délier la courroie de ses souliers.
texts.jhn.1.28: Ces choses se passèrent à Béthanie, au delà du Jourdain, où Jean baptisait.
texts.jhn.1.29: Le lendemain, il vit Jésus venant à lui, et il dit: Voici l'Agneau de Dieu, qui ôte le péché du monde.
texts.jhn.1.30: C'est celui dont j'ai dit: Après moi vient un homme qui m'a précédé, car il était avant moi.
texts.jhn.1.31: Je ne le connaissais pas, mais c'est afin qu'il fût manifesté à Israël que je suis venu baptiser d'eau.
texts.jhn.1.32: Jean rendit ce témoignage: J'ai vu l'Esprit descendre du ciel comme une colombe et s'arrêter sur lui.
texts.jhn.1.33: Je ne le connaissais pas, mais celui qui m'a envoyé baptiser d'eau, celui-là m'a dit: Celui sur qui tu verras l'Esprit descendre et s'arrêter, c'est celui qui baptise du Saint-Esprit.
texts.jhn.1.34: Et j'ai vu, et j'ai rendu témoignage qu'il est le Fils de Dieu.
texts.jhn.1.35: Le lendemain, Jean était encore là, avec deux de ses disciples;
texts.jhn.1.36: et, ayant regardé Jésus qui passait, il dit: Voilà l'Agneau de Dieu.
texts.jhn.1.37: Les deux disciples l'entendirent prononcer ces paroles, et ils suivirent Jésus.
texts.jhn.1.38: Jésus se retourna, et voyant qu'ils le suivaient, il leur dit: Que cherchez-vous? Ils lui répondirent: Rabbi ce qui signifie Maître, où demeures-tu?
texts.jhn.1.39: Venez, leur dit-il, et voyez. Ils allèrent, et ils virent où il demeurait; et ils restèrent auprès de lui ce jour-là. C'était environ la dixième heure.
texts.jhn.1.40: André, frère de Simon Pierre, était l'un des deux qui avaient entendu les paroles de Jean, et qui avaient suivi Jésus.
texts.jhn.1.41: Ce fut lui qui rencontra le premier son frère Simon, et il lui dit: Nous avons trouvé le Messie ce qui signifie Christ.
texts.jhn.1.42: Et il le conduisit vers Jésus. Jésus, l'ayant regardé, dit: Tu es Simon, fils de Jonas; tu seras appelé Céphas ce qui signifie Pierre.
texts.jhn.1.43: Le lendemain, Jésus voulut se rendre en Galilée, et il rencontra Philippe. Il lui dit: Suis-moi.
texts.jhn.1.44: Philippe était de Bethsaïda, de la ville d'André et de Pierre.
texts.jhn.1.45: Philippe rencontra Nathanaël, et lui dit: Nous avons trouvé celui de qui Moïse a écrit dans la loi et dont les prophètes ont parlé, Jésus de Nazareth, fils de Joseph.
texts.jhn.1.46: Nathanaël lui dit: Peut-il venir de Nazareth quelque chose de bon? Philippe lui répondit: Viens, et vois.
texts.jhn.1.47: Jésus, voyant venir à lui Nathanaël, dit de lui: Voici vraiment un Israélite, dans lequel il n'y a point de fraude.
texts.jhn.1.48: D'où me connais-tu? lui dit Nathanaël. Jésus lui répondit: Avant que Philippe t'appelât, quand tu étais sous le figuier, je t'ai vu.
texts.jhn.1.49: Nathanaël répondit et lui dit: Rabbi, tu es le Fils de Dieu, tu es le roi d'Israël.
texts.jhn.1.50: Jésus lui répondit: Parce que je t'ai dit que je t'ai vu sous le figuier, tu crois; tu verras de plus grandes choses que celles-ci.
texts.jhn.1.51: Et il lui dit: En vérité, en vérité, vous verrez désormais le ciel ouvert et les anges de Dieu monter et descendre sur le Fils de l'homme.
texts.jhn.2.1: Trois jours après, il y eut des noces à Cana en Galilée. La mère de Jésus était là,
texts.jhn.2.2: et Jésus fut aussi invité aux noces avec ses disciples.
texts.jhn.2.3: Le vin ayant manqué, la mère de Jésus lui dit: Ils n'ont plus de vin.
texts.jhn.2.4: Jésus lui répondit: Femme, qu'y a-t-il entre moi et toi? Mon heure n'est pas encore venue.
texts.jhn.2.5: Sa mère dit aux serviteurs: Faites ce qu'il vous dira.
texts.jhn.2.6: Or, il y avait là six vases de pierre, destinés aux purifications des Juifs, et contenant chacun deux ou trois mesures.
texts.jhn.2.7: Jésus leur dit: Remplissez d'eau ces vases. Et ils les remplirent jusqu'au bord.
texts.jhn.2.8: Puisez maintenant, leur dit-il, et portez-en à l'ordonnateur du repas. Et ils en portèrent.
texts.jhn.2.9: Quand l'ordonnateur du repas eut goûté l'eau changée en vin,-ne sachant d'où venait ce vin, tandis que les serviteurs, qui avaient puisé l'eau, le savaient bien, -il appela l'époux,
texts.jhn.2.10: et lui dit: Tout homme sert d'abord le bon vin, puis le moins bon après qu'on s'est enivré; toi, tu as gardé le bon vin jusqu'à présent.
texts.jhn.2.11: Tel fut, à Cana en Galilée, le premier des miracles que fit Jésus. Il manifesta sa gloire, et ses disciples crurent en lui.
texts.jhn.2.12: Après cela, il descendit à Capernaüm, avec sa mère, ses frères et ses disciples, et ils n'y demeurèrent que peu de jours.
texts.jhn.2.13: La Pâque des Juifs était proche, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.
texts.jhn.2.14: Il trouva dans le temple les vendeurs de boeufs, de brebis et de pigeons, et les changeurs assis.
texts.jhn.2.15: Ayant fait un fouet avec des cordes, il les chassa tous du temple, ainsi que les brebis et les boeufs; il dispersa la monnaie des changeurs, et renversa les tables;
texts.jhn.2.16: et il dit aux vendeurs de pigeons: Otez cela d'ici, ne faites pas de la maison de mon Père une maison de trafic.
texts.jhn.2.17: Ses disciples se souvinrent qu'il est écrit: Le zèle de ta maison me dévore.
texts.jhn.2.18: Les Juifs, prenant la parole, lui dirent: Quel miracle nous montres-tu, pour agir de la sorte?
texts.jhn.2.19: Jésus leur répondit: Détruisez ce temple, et en trois jours je le relèverai.
texts.jhn.2.20: Les Juifs dirent: Il a fallu quarante-six ans pour bâtir ce temple, et toi, en trois jours tu le relèveras!
texts.jhn.2.21: Mais il parlait du temple de son corps.
texts.jhn.2.22: C'est pourquoi, lorsqu'il fut ressuscité des morts, ses disciples se souvinrent qu'il avait dit cela, et ils crurent à l'Ecriture et à la parole que Jésus avait dite.
texts.jhn.2.23: Pendant que Jésus était à Jérusalem, à la fête de Pâque, plusieurs crurent en son nom, voyant les miracles qu'il faisait.
texts.jhn.2.24: Mais Jésus ne se fiait point à eux, parce qu'il les connaissait tous,
texts.jhn.2.25: et parce qu'il n'avait pas besoin qu'on lui rendît témoignage d'aucun homme; car il savait lui-même ce qui était dans l'homme.
texts.jhn.3.1: Mais il y eut un homme d'entre les pharisiens, nommé Nicodème, un chef des Juifs,
texts.jhn.3.2: qui vint, lui, auprès de Jésus, de nuit, et lui dit: Rabbi, nous savons que tu es un docteur venu de Dieu; car personne ne peut faire ces miracles que tu fais, si Dieu n'est avec lui.
texts.jhn.3.3: Jésus lui répondit: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis, si un homme ne naît de nouveau, il ne peut voir le royaume de Dieu.
texts.jhn.3.4: Nicodème lui dit: Comment un homme peut-il naître quand il est vieux? Peut-il rentrer dans le sein de sa mère et naître?
texts.jhn.3.5: Jésus répondit: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis, si un homme ne naît d'eau et d'Esprit, il ne peut entrer dans le royaume de Dieu.
texts.jhn.3.6: Ce qui est né de la chair est chair, et ce qui est né de l'Esprit est esprit.
texts.jhn.3.7: Ne t'étonne pas que je t'aie dit: Il faut que vous naissiez de nouveau.
texts.jhn.3.8: Le vent souffle où il veut, et tu en entends le bruit; mais tu ne sais d'où il vient, ni où il va. Il en est ainsi de tout homme qui est né de l'Esprit.
texts.jhn.3.9: Nicodème lui dit: Comment cela peut-il se faire?
texts.jhn.3.10: Jésus lui répondit: Tu es le docteur d'Israël, et tu ne sais pas ces choses!
texts.jhn.3.11: En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis, nous disons ce que nous savons, et nous rendons témoignage de ce que nous avons vu; et vous ne recevez pas notre témoignage.
texts.jhn.3.12: Si vous ne croyez pas quand je vous ai parlé des choses terrestres, comment croirez-vous quand je vous parlerai des choses célestes?
texts.jhn.3.13: Personne n'est monté au ciel, si ce n'est celui qui est descendu du ciel, le Fils de l'homme qui est dans le ciel.
texts.jhn.3.14: Et comme Moïse éleva le serpent dans le désert, il faut de même que le Fils de l'homme soit élevé,
texts.jhn.3.15: afin que quiconque croit en lui ait la vie éternelle.
texts.jhn.3.16: Car Dieu a tant aimé le monde qu'il a donné son Fils unique, afin que quiconque croit en lui ne périsse point, mais qu'il ait la vie éternelle.
texts.jhn.3.17: Dieu, en effet, n'a pas envoyé son Fils dans le monde pour qu'il juge le monde, mais pour que le monde soit sauvé par lui.
texts.jhn.3.18: Celui qui croit en lui n'est point jugé; mais celui qui ne croit pas est déjà jugé, parce qu'il n'a pas cru au nom du Fils unique de Dieu.
texts.jhn.3.19: Et ce jugement c'est que, la lumière étant venue dans le monde, les hommes ont préféré les ténèbres à la lumière, parce que leurs oeuvres étaient mauvaises.
texts.jhn.3.20: Car quiconque fait le mal hait la lumière, et ne vient point à la lumière, de peur que ses oeuvres ne soient dévoilées;
texts.jhn.3.21: mais celui qui agit selon la vérité vient à la lumière, afin que ses oeuvres soient manifestées, parce qu'elles sont faites en Dieu.
texts.jhn.3.22: Après cela, Jésus, accompagné de ses disciples, se rendit dans la terre de Judée; et là il demeurait avec eux, et il baptisait.
texts.jhn.3.23: Jean aussi baptisait à Enon, près de Salim, parce qu'il y avait là beaucoup d'eau; et on y venait pour être baptisé.
texts.jhn.3.24: Car Jean n'avait pas encore été mis en prison.
texts.jhn.3.25: Or, il s'éleva de la part des disciples de Jean une dispute avec un Juif touchant la purification.
texts.jhn.3.26: Ils vinrent trouver Jean, et lui dirent: Rabbi, celui qui était avec toi au delà du Jourdain, et à qui tu as rendu témoignage, voici, il baptise, et tous vont à lui.
texts.jhn.3.27: Jean répondit: Un homme ne peut recevoir que ce qui lui a été donné du ciel.
texts.jhn.3.28: Vous-mêmes m'êtes témoins que j'ai dit: Je ne suis pas le Christ, mais j'ai été envoyé devant lui.
texts.jhn.3.29: Celui à qui appartient l'épouse, c'est l'époux; mais l'ami de l'époux, qui se tient là et qui l'entend, éprouve une grande joie à cause de la voix de l'époux: aussi cette joie, qui est la mienne, est parfaite.
texts.jhn.3.30: Il faut qu'il croisse, et que je diminue.
texts.jhn.3.31: Celui qui vient d'en haut est au-dessus de tous; celui qui est de la terre est de la terre, et il parle comme étant de la terre. Celui qui vient du ciel est au-dessus de tous,
texts.jhn.3.32: il rend témoignage de ce qu'il a vu et entendu, et personne ne reçoit son témoignage.
texts.jhn.3.33: Celui qui a reçu son témoignage a certifié que Dieu est vrai;
texts.jhn.3.34: car celui que Dieu a envoyé dit les paroles de Dieu, parce que Dieu ne lui donne pas l'Esprit avec mesure.
texts.jhn.3.35: Le Père aime le Fils, et il a remis toutes choses entre ses mains.
texts.jhn.3.36: Celui qui croit au Fils a la vie éternelle; celui qui ne croit pas au Fils ne verra point la vie, mais la colère de Dieu demeure sur lui.
texts.jhn.4.1: Le Seigneur sut que les pharisiens avaient appris qu'il faisait et baptisait plus de disciples que Jean.
texts.jhn.4.2: Toutefois Jésus ne baptisait pas lui-même, mais c'étaient ses disciples.
texts.jhn.4.3: Alors il quitta la Judée, et retourna en Galilée.
texts.jhn.4.4: Comme il fallait qu'il passât par la Samarie,
texts.jhn.4.5: il arriva dans une ville de Samarie, nommée Sychar, près du champ que Jacob avait donné à Joseph, son fils.
texts.jhn.4.6: Là se trouvait le puits de Jacob. Jésus, fatigué du voyage, était assis au bord du puits. C'était environ la sixième heure.
texts.jhn.4.7: Une femme de Samarie vint puiser de l'eau. Jésus lui dit: Donne-moi à boire.
texts.jhn.4.8: Car ses disciples étaient allés à la ville pour acheter des vivres.
texts.jhn.4.9: La femme samaritaine lui dit: Comment toi, qui es Juif, me demandes-tu à boire, à moi qui suis une femme samaritaine? -Les Juifs, en effet, n'ont pas de relations avec les Samaritains. -
texts.jhn.4.10: Jésus lui répondit: Si tu connaissais le don de Dieu et qui est celui qui te dit: Donne-moi à boire! tu lui aurais toi-même demandé à boire, et il t'aurait donné de l'eau vive.
texts.jhn.4.11: Seigneur, lui dit la femme, tu n'as rien pour puiser, et le puits est profond; d'où aurais-tu donc cette eau vive?
texts.jhn.4.12: Es-tu plus grand que notre père Jacob, qui nous a donné ce puits, et qui en a bu lui-même, ainsi que ses fils et ses troupeaux?
texts.jhn.4.13: Jésus lui répondit: Quiconque boit de cette eau aura encore soif;
texts.jhn.4.14: mais celui qui boira de l'eau que je lui donnerai n'aura jamais soif, et l'eau que je lui donnerai deviendra en lui une source d'eau qui jaillira jusque dans la vie éternelle.
texts.jhn.4.15: La femme lui dit: Seigneur, donne-moi cette eau, afin que je n'aie plus soif, et que je ne vienne plus puiser ici.
texts.jhn.4.16: Va, lui dit Jésus, appelle ton mari, et viens ici.
texts.jhn.4.17: La femme répondit: Je n'ai point de mari. Jésus lui dit: Tu as eu raison de dire: Je n'ai point de mari.
texts.jhn.4.18: Car tu as eu cinq maris, et celui que tu as maintenant n'est pas ton mari. En cela tu as dit vrai.
texts.jhn.4.19: Seigneur, lui dit la femme, je vois que tu es prophète.
texts.jhn.4.20: Nos pères ont adoré sur cette montagne; et vous dites, vous, que le lieu où il faut adorer est à Jérusalem.
texts.jhn.4.21: Femme, lui dit Jésus, crois-moi, l'heure vient où ce ne sera ni sur cette montagne ni à Jérusalem que vous adorerez le Père.
texts.jhn.4.22: Vous adorez ce que vous ne connaissez pas; nous, nous adorons ce que nous connaissons, car le salut vient des Juifs.
texts.jhn.4.23: Mais l'heure vient, et elle est déjà venue, où les vrais adorateurs adoreront le Père en esprit et en vérité; car ce sont là les adorateurs que le Père demande.
texts.jhn.4.24: Dieu est Esprit, et il faut que ceux qui l'adorent l'adorent en esprit et en vérité.
texts.jhn.4.25: La femme lui dit: Je sais que le Messie doit venir celui qu'on appelle Christ; quand il sera venu, il nous annoncera toutes choses.
texts.jhn.4.26: Jésus lui dit: Je le suis, moi qui te parle.
texts.jhn.4.27: Là-dessus arrivèrent ses disciples, qui furent étonnés de ce qu'il parlait avec une femme. Toutefois aucun ne dit: Que demandes-tu? ou: De quoi parles-tu avec elle?
texts.jhn.4.28: Alors la femme, ayant laissé sa cruche, s'en alla dans la ville, et dit aux gens:
texts.jhn.4.29: Venez voir un homme qui m'a dit tout ce que j'ai fait; ne serait-ce point le Christ?
texts.jhn.4.30: Ils sortirent de la ville, et ils vinrent vers lui.
texts.jhn.4.31: Pendant ce temps, les disciples le pressaient de manger, disant: Rabbi, mange.
texts.jhn.4.32: Mais il leur dit: J'ai à manger une nourriture que vous ne connaissez pas.
texts.jhn.4.33: Les disciples se disaient donc les uns aux autres: Quelqu'un lui aurait-il apporté à manger?
texts.jhn.4.34: Jésus leur dit: Ma nourriture est de faire la volonté de celui qui m'a envoyé, et d'accomplir son oeuvre.
texts.jhn.4.35: Ne dites-vous pas qu'il y a encore quatre mois jusqu'à la moisson? Voici, je vous le dis, levez les yeux, et regardez les champs qui déjà blanchissent pour la moisson.
texts.jhn.4.36: Celui qui moissonne reçoit un salaire, et amasse des fruits pour la vie éternelle, afin que celui qui sème et celui qui moissonne se réjouissent ensemble.
texts.jhn.4.37: Car en ceci ce qu'on dit est vrai: Autre est celui qui sème, et autre celui qui moissonne.
texts.jhn.4.38: Je vous ai envoyés moissonner ce que vous n'avez pas travaillé; d'autres ont travaillé, et vous êtes entrés dans leur travail.
texts.jhn.4.39: Plusieurs Samaritains de cette ville crurent en Jésus à cause de cette déclaration formelle de la femme: Il m'a dit tout ce que j'ai fait.
texts.jhn.4.40: Aussi, quand les Samaritains vinrent le trouver, ils le prièrent de rester auprès d'eux. Et il resta là deux jours.
texts.jhn.4.41: Un beaucoup plus grand nombre crurent à cause de sa parole;
texts.jhn.4.42: et ils disaient à la femme: Ce n'est plus à cause de ce que tu as dit que nous croyons; car nous l'avons entendu nous-mêmes, et nous savons qu'il est vraiment le Sauveur du monde.
texts.jhn.4.43: Après ces deux jours, Jésus partit de là, pour se rendre en Galilée;
texts.jhn.4.44: car il avait déclaré lui-même qu'un prophète n'est pas honoré dans sa propre patrie.
texts.jhn.4.45: Lorsqu'il arriva en Galilée, il fut bien reçu des Galiléens, qui avaient vu tout ce qu'il avait fait à Jérusalem pendant la fête; car eux aussi étaient allés à la fête.
texts.jhn.4.46: Il retourna donc à Cana en Galilée, où il avait changé l'eau en vin. Il y avait à Capernaüm un officier du roi, dont le fils était malade.
texts.jhn.4.47: Ayant appris que Jésus était venu de Judée en Galilée, il alla vers lui, et le pria de descendre et de guérir son fils, qui était près de mourir.
texts.jhn.4.48: Jésus lui dit: Si vous ne voyez des miracles et des prodiges, vous ne croyez point.
texts.jhn.4.49: L'officier du roi lui dit: Seigneur, descends avant que mon enfant meure.
texts.jhn.4.50: Va, lui dit Jésus, ton fils vit. Et cet homme crut à la parole que Jésus lui avait dite, et il s'en alla.
texts.jhn.4.51: Comme déjà il descendait, ses serviteurs venant à sa rencontre, lui apportèrent cette nouvelle: Ton enfant vit.
texts.jhn.4.52: Il leur demanda à quelle heure il s'était trouvé mieux; et ils lui dirent: Hier, à la septième heure, la fièvre l'a quitté.
texts.jhn.4.53: Le père reconnut que c'était à cette heure-là que Jésus lui avait dit: Ton fils vit. Et il crut, lui et toute sa maison.
texts.jhn.4.54: Jésus fit encore ce second miracle lorsqu'il fut venu de Judée en Galilée.
texts.jhn.5.1: Après cela, il y eut une fête des Juifs, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.
texts.jhn.5.2: Or, à Jérusalem, près de la porte des brebis, il y a une piscine qui s'appelle en hébreu Béthesda, et qui a cinq portiques.
texts.jhn.5.3: Sous ces portiques étaient couchés en grand nombre des malades, des aveugles, des boiteux, des paralytiques, qui attendaient le mouvement de l'eau;
texts.jhn.5.4: car un ange descendait de temps en temps dans la piscine, et agitait l'eau; et celui qui y descendait le premier après que l'eau avait été agitée était guéri, quelle que fût sa maladie.
texts.jhn.5.5: Là se trouvait un homme malade depuis trente-huit ans.
texts.jhn.5.6: Jésus, l'ayant vu couché, et sachant qu'il était malade depuis longtemps, lui dit: Veux-tu être guéri?
texts.jhn.5.7: Le malade lui répondit: Seigneur, je n'ai personne pour me jeter dans la piscine quand l'eau est agitée, et, pendant que j'y vais, un autre descend avant moi.
texts.jhn.5.8: Lève-toi, lui dit Jésus, prends ton lit, et marche.
texts.jhn.5.9: Aussitôt cet homme fut guéri; il prit son lit, et marcha. C'était un jour de sabbat.
texts.jhn.5.10: Les Juifs dirent donc à celui qui avait été guéri: C'est le sabbat; il ne t'est pas permis d'emporter ton lit.
texts.jhn.5.11: Il leur répondit: Celui qui m'a guéri m'a dit: Prends ton lit, et marche.
