texts.jhn.13.2: And supper being ended (the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray him;)
texts.jhn.13.3: Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God, and was going to God;
texts.jhn.13.4: He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.
texts.jhn.13.5: After that, he poured water into a basin, and began to wash the disciples feet, and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
texts.jhn.13.6: Then he cometh to Simon Peter: and Peter saith to him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?
texts.jhn.13.7: Jesus answered and said to him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter.
texts.jhn.13.8: Peter saith to him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
texts.jhn.13.9: Simon Peter saith to him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.
texts.jhn.13.10: Jesus saith to him, He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is wholly clean: and ye are clean, but not all.
texts.jhn.13.11: For he knew who would betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.
texts.jhn.13.12: So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he said to them, Know ye what I have done to you?
texts.jhn.13.13: Ye call me Master, and Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.
texts.jhn.13.14: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet.
texts.jhn.13.15: For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
texts.jhn.13.16: Verily, verily, I say to you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.
texts.jhn.13.17: If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
texts.jhn.13.18: I speak not of you all; I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth bread with me, hath lifted up his heel against me.
texts.jhn.13.19: Now I tell you before it cometh, that when it hath come to pass, ye may believe that I am he.
texts.jhn.13.20: Verily, verily, I say to you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send, receiveth me; and he that receiveth me, receiveth him that sent me.
texts.jhn.13.21: When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say to you, that one of you will betray me.
texts.jhn.13.22: Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spoke.
texts.jhn.13.23: Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom, one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
texts.jhn.13.24: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, to ask who it should be of whom he spoke.
texts.jhn.13.25: He then lying on Jesus' breast, saith to him, Lord, who is it?
texts.jhn.13.26: Jesus answered, He it is to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
texts.jhn.13.27: And after the sop Satan entered into him. Then said Jesus to him, What thou doest, do quickly.
texts.jhn.13.28: Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spoke this to him.
texts.jhn.13.29: For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said to him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.
texts.jhn.13.30: He then having received the sop, went immediately out: and it was night.
texts.jhn.13.31: Therefore when he had gone out, Jesus said, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.
texts.jhn.13.32: If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will immediately glorify him.
texts.jhn.13.33: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye will seek me: and, as I said to the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say to you.
texts.jhn.13.34: A new commandment I give to you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.
texts.jhn.13.35: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
texts.jhn.13.36: Simon Peter said to him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterward.
texts.jhn.13.37: Peter said to him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thy sake.
texts.jhn.13.38: Jesus answered him, Wilt thou lay down thy life for my sake? Verily, verily, I say to thee, The cock will not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.
texts.jhn.14.1: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
texts.jhn.14.2: In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
texts.jhn.14.3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
texts.jhn.14.4: And whither I go ye know, and the way ye know.
texts.jhn.14.5: Thomas saith to him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?
texts.jhn.14.6: Jesus saith to him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no man cometh to the Father, but by me.
texts.jhn.14.7: If ye had known me, ye would have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
texts.jhn.14.8: Philip saith to him, Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us.
texts.jhn.14.9: Jesus saith to him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me Philip? he that hath seen me, hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Show us the Father?
texts.jhn.14.10: Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I speak to you, I speak not from myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works.
texts.jhn.14.11: Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works' sake.
texts.jhn.14.12: Verily, verily, I say to you, he that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go to my Father.
texts.jhn.14.13: And whatever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
texts.jhn.14.14: If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it.
texts.jhn.14.15: If ye love me, keep my commandments.
texts.jhn.14.16: And I will pray the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever;
texts.jhn.14.17: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and will be in you.
texts.jhn.14.18: I will not leave you comfortless; I will come to you.
texts.jhn.14.19: Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also.
texts.jhn.14.20: At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.
texts.jhn.14.21: He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me, shall be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.
texts.jhn.14.22: Judas, not Iscariot, saith to him, Lord, how is it that thou wilt manifest thyself to us, and not to the world?
texts.jhn.14.23: Jesus answered and said to him, If a man loveth me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our abode with him.
texts.jhn.14.24: He that loveth me not, keepeth not my sayings: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but that of the Father who sent me.
texts.jhn.14.25: These things have I spoken to you, being yet present with you.
texts.jhn.14.26: But the Comforter, who is the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatever I have said to you.
texts.jhn.14.27: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you: not as the world giveth, give I to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
texts.jhn.14.28: Ye have heard that I said to you, I go away, and come again to you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go to the Father: for my Father is greater than I.
texts.jhn.14.29: And now I have told you before it cometh to pass, that when it hath come to pass, ye may believe.
texts.jhn.14.30: Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the prince of this world cometh, and hath nothing in me.
texts.jhn.14.31: But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.
texts.jhn.15.1: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
texts.jhn.15.2: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he taketh away; and every branch that beareth fruit, he cleaneth it, that it my bring forth more fruit.
texts.jhn.15.3: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.
texts.jhn.15.4: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine: no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
texts.jhn.15.5: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
texts.jhn.15.6: If a man abideth not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered: and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
texts.jhn.15.7: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye may ask what ye will, and it shall be done to you.
texts.jhn.15.8: In this is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
texts.jhn.15.9: As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.
texts.jhn.15.10: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
texts.jhn.15.11: These things have I spoken to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be full.
texts.jhn.15.12: This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you.
texts.jhn.15.13: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
texts.jhn.15.14: Ye are my friends, if ye do whatever I command you.
texts.jhn.15.15: Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard from my Father, I have made known to you.
texts.jhn.15.16: Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
texts.jhn.15.17: These things I command you, that ye love one another.
texts.jhn.15.18: If the world hateth you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
texts.jhn.15.19: If ye were of the world, the world would love its own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
texts.jhn.15.20: Remember the word that I said to you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you: if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
texts.jhn.15.21: But all these things will they do to you for my name's sake, because they know not him that sent me.
texts.jhn.15.22: If I had not come and spoken to them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin.
texts.jhn.15.23: He that hateth me, hateth my Father also.
texts.jhn.15.24: If I had not done among them the works which no other man hath done, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen, and hated both me and my Father.
texts.jhn.15.25: But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
texts.jhn.15.26: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send to you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, who proceedeth from the Father, he will testify concerning me.
texts.jhn.15.27: And ye also shall bear testimony, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
texts.jhn.16.1: These things have I spoken to you, that ye should not be offended.
texts.jhn.16.2: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yes, the time cometh, that whoever killeth you, will think that he doeth God service.
texts.jhn.16.3: And these things will they do to you, because they have not known the Father, nor me.
texts.jhn.16.4: But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not to you at the beginning, because I was with you.
texts.jhn.16.5: But now I go to him that sent me, and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
texts.jhn.16.6: But because I have said these things to you, sorrow hath filled your heart.
texts.jhn.16.7: Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: It is expedient for you that I depart; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come to you; but if I depart, I will send him to you.
texts.jhn.16.8: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
texts.jhn.16.9: Of sin, because they believe not on me;
texts.jhn.16.10: Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;
texts.jhn.16.11: Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.
texts.jhn.16.12: I have yet many things to say to you, but ye cannot bear them now.
texts.jhn.16.13: But, when he, the Spirit of truth is come, he will guide you into all the truth: for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he shall hear, that will he speak: and he will show you things to come.
texts.jhn.16.14: He will glorify me: for he will receive of mine, and will show it to you.
texts.jhn.16.15: All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore I said, that he will take of mine, and show it to you.
texts.jhn.16.16: A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me, because I go to the Father.
texts.jhn.16.17: Then said some of his disciples among themselves, What is this that he saith to us, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?
texts.jhn.16.18: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? we cannot tell what he saith.
texts.jhn.16.19: Now Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, and said to them, Do ye inquire among yourselves of that which I said, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me?
texts.jhn.16.20: Verily, verily, I say to you, that ye will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice: and ye will be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.
texts.jhn.16.21: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world.
texts.jhn.16.22: And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
texts.jhn.16.23: And in that day ye will ask me nothing: Verily, verily, I say to you, Whatever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.
texts.jhn.16.24: Hitherto ye have asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full.
texts.jhn.16.25: These things have I spoken to you in proverbs: but the time cometh when I shall no more speak to you in proverbs, but I shall show you plainly concerning the Father.
texts.jhn.16.26: At that day ye will ask in my name: and I say not to you, that I will pray the Father for you:
texts.jhn.16.27: For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came from God.
texts.jhn.16.28: I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.
texts.jhn.16.29: His disciples said to him, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no proverb.
texts.jhn.16.30: Now are we sure that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest from God.
texts.jhn.16.31: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?
texts.jhn.16.32: Behold, the hour cometh, and is even now come, that ye shall be scattered every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
texts.jhn.16.33: These things I have spoken to you, that in me ye may have peace. In the world ye will have tribulation, but be of good cheer: I have overcome the world.
texts.jhn.17.1: These words spoke Jesus, and lifted up his eyes to heaven, and said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee:
texts.jhn.17.2: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him.
texts.jhn.17.3: And this is life eternal, that they may know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent.
texts.jhn.17.4: I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
texts.jhn.17.5: And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thy ownself, with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
texts.jhn.17.6: I have manifested thy name to the men whom thou gavest to me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept thy word.
texts.jhn.17.7: Now they have known that all things whatever thou hast given me are from thee.
texts.jhn.17.8: For I have given to them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me.
texts.jhn.17.9: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them whom thou hast given to me; for they are thine.
texts.jhn.17.10: And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them.
texts.jhn.17.11: And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thy own name those whom thou hast given to me, that they may be one, as we are.
texts.jhn.17.12: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest to me I have kept, and none of them is lost but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.
texts.jhn.17.13: And now I come to thee, and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
texts.jhn.17.14: I have given to them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
texts.jhn.17.15: I pray not that thou shouldst take them out of the world, but that thou shouldst keep them from the evil.
texts.jhn.17.16: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
texts.jhn.17.17: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
texts.jhn.17.18: As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.
texts.jhn.17.19: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified through the truth.
texts.jhn.17.20: Neither pray I for these alone; but for them also who shall believe on me through their word.
texts.jhn.17.21: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
texts.jhn.17.22: And the glory which thou gavest to me, I have given to them; that they may be one, even as we are one.
texts.jhn.17.23: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them as thou hast loved me.
texts.jhn.17.24: Father, I will that they also whom thou hast given to me be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory which thou hast given to me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
texts.jhn.17.25: O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.
texts.jhn.17.26: And I have declared to them thy name, and will declare it: that the love with which thou hast loved me, may be in them, and I in them.
texts.jhn.18.1: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Kedron, where was a garden, into which he entered, and his disciples.
texts.jhn.18.2: And Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus often resorted thither with his disciples.
texts.jhn.18.3: Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns, and torches, and weapons.
texts.jhn.18.4: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that were coming upon him, went forth, and said to them, Whom seek ye?
texts.jhn.18.5: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith to them, I am he. And Judas also, who betrayed him, stood with them.
texts.jhn.18.6: As soon then as he had said to them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground.
texts.jhn.18.7: Then he asked them again, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.
texts.jhn.18.8: Jesus answered, I have told you that I am he: If therefore ye seek me, let these go away:
texts.jhn.18.9: That the saying might be fulfilled which he spoke, Of them whom thou gavest to me, I have lost none.
texts.jhn.18.10: Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it, and smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
texts.jhn.18.11: Then said Jesus to Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?
texts.jhn.18.12: Then the band, and the captain, and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him,
texts.jhn.18.13: And led him away to Annas first, (for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was the high priest that same year.)
texts.jhn.18.14: Now Caiaphas was he who gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
texts.jhn.18.15: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.
texts.jhn.18.16: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple who was known to the high priest, and spoke to her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.
texts.jhn.18.17: Then saith the damsel that kept the door to Peter, Art not thou also one of this man's disciples? He saith, I am not.
texts.jhn.18.18: And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; (for it was cold) and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.
texts.jhn.18.19: The high priest then asked Jesus concerning his disciples, and concerning his doctrine.
texts.jhn.18.20: Jesus answered him, I spoke openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.
texts.jhn.18.21: Why dost thou ask me? ask them who heard me, what I have said to them: behold, they know what I have said.
texts.jhn.18.22: And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers who stood by, struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?
texts.jhn.18.23: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear testimony of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?
texts.jhn.18.24: (Now Annas had sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.)
texts.jhn.18.25: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore to him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it, and said, I am not.
texts.jhn.18.26: One of the servants of the high priest (being the kinsman of him whose ear Peter cut off) saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?
texts.jhn.18.27: Peter then denied again, and immediately the cock crowed.
texts.jhn.18.28: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment-hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover.
texts.jhn.18.29: Pilate then went out to them, and said, What accusation bring ye against this man?
texts.jhn.18.30: They answered and said to him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee.
texts.jhn.18.31: Then said Pilate to them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said to him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:
texts.jhn.18.32: That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying what death he should die.
texts.jhn.18.33: Then Pilate entered into the judgment-hall again, and called Jesus, and said to him, Art thou the King of the Jews?
texts.jhn.18.34: Jesus answered him, Sayest thou this thing from thyself, or did others tell it thee concerning me?
texts.jhn.18.35: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thy own nation, and the chief priests, have delivered thee to me: What hast thou done?
texts.jhn.18.36: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.
texts.jhn.18.37: Pilate therefore said to him, Art thou a King then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a King. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should testify to the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.
texts.jhn.18.38: Pilate saith to him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again to the Jews, and saith to them, I find in him no fault.
texts.jhn.18.39: But ye have a custom that I should release to you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release to you the King of the Jews?
texts.jhn.18.40: Then they all cried again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.
texts.jhn.19.1: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.
texts.jhn.19.2: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,
texts.jhn.19.3: And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.
texts.jhn.19.4: Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith to them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.
texts.jhn.19.5: Then Jesus came forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith to them, Behold the man!
texts.jhn.19.6: When therefore the chief priests and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. Pilate saith to them, Take ye him, and crucify him: for I find no fault in him.
texts.jhn.19.7: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.
texts.jhn.19.8: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid;
texts.jhn.19.9: And went again into the judgment-hall, and saith to Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.
texts.jhn.19.10: Then saith Pilate to him, Speakest thou not to me? knowest thou not, that I have power to crucify thee, and have power to release thee?
texts.jhn.19.11: Jesus answered, Thou couldst have no power against me; except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me to thee hath the greater sin.
texts.jhn.19.12: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar's friend. Whoever maketh himself a king, speaketh against Cesar.
texts.jhn.19.13: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down on the judgment-seat, in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.
texts.jhn.19.14: And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith to the Jews, Behold your King!
texts.jhn.19.15: But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith to them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.
texts.jhn.19.16: Then therefore he delivered him to them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.
texts.jhn.19.17: And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew, Golgotha:
texts.jhn.19.18: Where they crucified him, and two others with him, on each side one, and Jesus in the midst.
texts.jhn.19.19: And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.jhn.19.20: Many of the Jews then read this title: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
texts.jhn.19.21: Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.
texts.jhn.19.22: Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.
texts.jhn.19.23: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also his coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.
texts.jhn.19.24: They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.
texts.jhn.19.25: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus, his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
texts.jhn.19.26: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith to his mother, Woman, behold thy son!
texts.jhn.19.27: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her to his own home.
texts.jhn.19.28: After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst.
texts.jhn.19.29: Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a spunge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth.
texts.jhn.19.30: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and expired.
texts.jhn.19.31: The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath, (for that sabbath was a great day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.
texts.jhn.19.32: Then came the soldiers, and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him.
texts.jhn.19.33: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they broke not his legs:
texts.jhn.19.34: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came out blood and water.
texts.jhn.19.35: And he that saw it, testified, and his testimony is true: and he knoweth that he speaketh truth, that ye may believe.
texts.jhn.19.36: For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.
texts.jhn.19.37: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.
texts.jhn.19.38: And after this, Joseph of Arimathea (being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews) besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore and took the body of Jesus.
texts.jhn.19.39: And there came also Nicodemus (who at the first came to Jesus by night) and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pound weight.
texts.jhn.19.40: Then they took the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen cloths, with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.
texts.jhn.19.41: Now in the place where he was crucified, there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulcher, in which was never man yet laid.
texts.jhn.19.42: There they laid Jesus therefore, because of the Jews' preparation-day, for the sepulcher was nigh at hand.
texts.jhn.20.1: The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, to the sepulcher, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulcher.
texts.jhn.20.2: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and saith to them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulcher, and we know not where they have laid him.
texts.jhn.20.3: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulcher.
texts.jhn.20.4: So they ran both together: and the other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the sepulcher.
texts.jhn.20.5: And he stooping down, saw the linen cloths lying; yet he went not in.
texts.jhn.20.6: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulcher, and seeth the linen cloths lying;
texts.jhn.20.7: And the napkin that was about his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but wrapped together in a place by itself.
texts.jhn.20.8: Then went in also that other disciple who came first to the sepulcher, and he saw, and believed.
texts.jhn.20.9: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
texts.jhn.20.10: Then the disciples went away again to their own home.
texts.jhn.20.11: But Mary stood without at the sepulcher weeping: and as she wept she stooped down to look into the sepulcher,
texts.jhn.20.12: And seeth two angels in white, sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
texts.jhn.20.13: And they say to her, Woman, why weepest thou? she saith to them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.
texts.jhn.20.14: And when she had thus said, she turned herself about, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.
texts.jhn.20.15: Jesus saith to her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith to him, Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
texts.jhn.20.16: Jesus saith to her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith to him, Rabboni, which is to say, Master.
texts.jhn.20.17: Jesus saith to her, Touch me not: for I have not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say to them, I ascend to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.
texts.jhn.20.18: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken these things to her.
texts.jhn.20.19: Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith to them, Peace be to you.
texts.jhn.20.20: And when he had so said, he showed to them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad when they saw the Lord.
texts.jhn.20.21: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be to you: as my Father hath sent me, even so I send you.
texts.jhn.20.22: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith to them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit.
texts.jhn.20.23: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted to them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.
texts.jhn.20.24: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
texts.jhn.20.25: The other disciples therefore said to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.
texts.jhn.20.26: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be to you.
texts.jhn.20.27: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side; and be not faithless, but believing.
texts.jhn.20.28: And Thomas answered and said to him, My Lord and my God.
texts.jhn.20.29: Jesus saith to him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
texts.jhn.20.30: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
texts.jhn.20.31: But these are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing ye may have life through his name.
texts.jhn.21.1: After these things Jesus showed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias: and in this manner did he show himself.
texts.jhn.21.2: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.
texts.jhn.21.3: Simon Peter saith to them, I go a fishing. They say to him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a boat immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
texts.jhn.21.4: But when the morning had now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
texts.jhn.21.5: Then Jesus saith to them, Children, have ye any victuals? They answered him, No.
texts.jhn.21.6: And he said to them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
texts.jhn.21.7: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith to Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt on his fisher's coat, (for he was naked) and cast himself into the sea.
texts.jhn.21.8: And the other disciples came in a little boat (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits) dragging the net with fishes.
texts.jhn.21.9: As soon then as they had come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid upon them, and bread.
texts.jhn.21.10: Jesus saith to them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.
texts.jhn.21.11: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty and three: and notwithstanding there were so many, yet the net was not broken.
texts.jhn.21.12: Jesus saith to them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
texts.jhn.21.13: Jesus then cometh, and taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish likewise.
texts.jhn.21.14: This is now the third time that Jesus showed himself to his disciples, after he had risen from the dead.
texts.jhn.21.15: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith to him, Yes, Lord: thou knowest that I love thee. He saith to him, Feed my lambs.
texts.jhn.21.16: He saith to him again the second time, Simon son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith to him, Yes, Lord: thou knowest that I love thee. He saith to him, Feed my sheep.
texts.jhn.21.17: He saith to him the third time, Simon son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved, because he said to him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said to him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith to him, Feed my sheep.
texts.jhn.21.18: Verily, verily, I say to thee, When thou wast young, thou didst gird thyself and walk whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldst not.
texts.jhn.21.19: This he spoke, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith to him, Follow me.
texts.jhn.21.20: Then Peter turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved, following; (who also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, who is he that betrayeth thee?)
texts.jhn.21.21: Peter seeing him, saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
texts.jhn.21.22: Jesus saith to him, If I will that he shall tarry till I come, what is that to thee? Follow thou me.
texts.jhn.21.23: Then this saying went abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not to him, He shall not die; but, if I will that he shall tarry till I come, what is that to thee?
texts.jhn.21.24: This is the disciple who testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.
texts.jhn.21.25: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that would be written. Amen.

texts.jhn.1.1: In [the] beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
texts.jhn.1.2: *He* was in the beginning with God.
texts.jhn.1.3: All things received being through him, and without him not one [thing] received being which has received being.
texts.jhn.1.4: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
texts.jhn.1.5: And the light appears in darkness, and the darkness apprehended it not.
texts.jhn.1.6: There was a man sent from God, his name John.
texts.jhn.1.7: He came for witness, that he might witness concerning the light, that all might believe through him.
texts.jhn.1.8: *He* was not the light, but that he might witness concerning the light.
texts.jhn.1.9: The true light was that which, coming into the world, lightens every man.
texts.jhn.1.10: He was in the world, and the world had [its] being through him, and the world knew him not.
texts.jhn.1.11: He came to his own, and his own received him not;
texts.jhn.1.12: but as many as received him, to them gave he [the] right to be children of God, to those that believe on his name;
texts.jhn.1.13: who have been born, not of blood, nor of flesh's will, nor of man's will, but of God.
texts.jhn.1.14: And the Word became flesh, and dwelt among us (and we have contemplated his glory, a glory as of an only-begotten with a father), full of grace and truth;
texts.jhn.1.15: (John bears witness of him, and he has cried, saying, This was he of whom I said, He that comes after me is preferred before me, for he was before me;)
texts.jhn.1.16: for of his fulness we all have received, and grace upon grace.
texts.jhn.1.17: For the law was given by Moses: grace and truth subsists through Jesus Christ.
texts.jhn.1.18: No one has seen God at any time; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, *he* hath declared [him].
texts.jhn.1.19: And this is the witness of John, when the Jews sent from Jerusalem priests and Levites that they might ask him, Thou, who art thou?
texts.jhn.1.20: And he acknowledged and denied not, and acknowledged, I am not the Christ.
texts.jhn.1.21: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias? And he says, I am not. Art thou the prophet? And he answered, No.
texts.jhn.1.22: They said therefore to him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?
texts.jhn.1.23: He said, I [am] [the] voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the path of [the] Lord, as said Esaias the prophet.
texts.jhn.1.24: And they were sent from among the Pharisees.
texts.jhn.1.25: And they asked him and said to him, Why baptisest thou then, if thou art not the Christ, nor Elias, nor the prophet?
texts.jhn.1.26: John answered them saying, I baptise with water. In the midst of you stands, whom ye do not know,
texts.jhn.1.27: he who comes after me, the thong of whose sandal I am not worthy to unloose.
texts.jhn.1.28: These things took place in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptising.
texts.jhn.1.29: On the morrow he sees Jesus coming to him, and says, Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.
texts.jhn.1.30: He it is of whom I said, A man comes after me who takes a place before me, because he *was* before me;
texts.jhn.1.31: and I knew him not; but that he might be manifested to Israel, therefore have I come baptising with water.
texts.jhn.1.32: And John bore witness, saying, I beheld the Spirit descending as a dove from heaven, and it abode upon him.
texts.jhn.1.33: And I knew him not; but he who sent me to baptise with water, *he* said to me, Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending and abiding on him, he it is who baptises with [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.jhn.1.34: And I have seen and borne witness that this is the Son of God.
texts.jhn.1.35: Again, on the morrow, there stood John and two of his disciples.
texts.jhn.1.36: And, looking at Jesus as he walked, he says, Behold the Lamb of God.
texts.jhn.1.37: And the two disciples heard him speaking, and followed Jesus.
texts.jhn.1.38: But Jesus having turned, and seeing them following, says to them, What seek ye? And *they* said to him, Rabbi (which, being interpreted, signifies Teacher), where abidest thou?
texts.jhn.1.39: He says to them, Come and see. They went therefore, and saw where he abode; and they abode with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
texts.jhn.1.40: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard [this] from John and followed him.
texts.jhn.1.41: He first finds his own brother Simon, and says to him, We have found the Messias (which being interpreted is Christ).
texts.jhn.1.42: And he led him to Jesus. Jesus looking at him said, Thou art Simon, the son of Jonas; thou shalt be called Cephas (which interpreted is stone).
texts.jhn.1.43: On the morrow he would go forth into Galilee, and Jesus finds Philip, and says to him, Follow me.
texts.jhn.1.44: And Philip was from Bethsaida, of the city of Andrew and Peter.
texts.jhn.1.45: Philip finds Nathanael, and says to him, We have found him of whom Moses wrote in the law, and the prophets, Jesus, the son of Joseph, who is from Nazareth.
texts.jhn.1.46: And Nathanael said to him, Can anything good come out of Nazareth? Philip says to him, Come and see.
texts.jhn.1.47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and says of him, Behold [one] truly an Israelite, in whom there is no guile.
texts.jhn.1.48: Nathanael says to him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said to him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig-tree, I saw thee.
texts.jhn.1.49: Nathanael answered and said to him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God, thou art the King of Israel.
texts.jhn.1.50: Jesus answered and said to him, Because I said to thee, I saw thee under the fig-tree, believest thou? Thou shalt see greater things than these.
texts.jhn.1.51: And he says to him, Verily, verily, I say to you, Henceforth ye shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of man.
texts.jhn.2.1: And on the third day a marriage took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
texts.jhn.2.2: And Jesus also, and his disciples, were invited to the marriage.
texts.jhn.2.3: And wine being deficient, the mother of Jesus says to him, They have no wine.
texts.jhn.2.4: Jesus says to her, What have I to do with thee, woman? mine hour has not yet come.
texts.jhn.2.5: His mother says to the servants, Whatever he may say to you, do.
texts.jhn.2.6: Now there were standing there six stone water-vessels, according to the purification of the Jews, holding two or three measures each.
texts.jhn.2.7: Jesus says to them, Fill the water-vessels with water. And they filled them up to the brim.
texts.jhn.2.8: And he says to them, Draw out now, and carry [it] to the feast-master. And they carried [it].
texts.jhn.2.9: But when the feast-master had tasted the water which had been made wine (and knew not whence it was, but the servants knew who drew the water), the feast-master calls the bridegroom,
texts.jhn.2.10: and says to him, Every man sets on first the good wine, and when [men] have well drunk, then the inferior; thou hast kept the good wine till now.
texts.jhn.2.11: This beginning of signs did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory; and his disciples believed on him.
texts.jhn.2.12: After this he descended to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brethren and his disciples; and there they abode not many days.
texts.jhn.2.13: And the passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
texts.jhn.2.14: And he found in the temple the sellers of oxen and sheep and doves, and the money-changers sitting;
texts.jhn.2.15: and, having made a scourge of cords, he cast [them] all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he poured out the change of the money-changers, and overturned the tables,
texts.jhn.2.16: and said to the sellers of doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father's house a house of merchandise.
texts.jhn.2.17: [And] his disciples remembered that it is written, The zeal of thy house devours me.
texts.jhn.2.18: The Jews therefore answered and said to him, What sign shewest thou to us, that thou doest these things?
texts.jhn.2.19: Jesus answered and said to them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
texts.jhn.2.20: The Jews therefore said, Forty and six years was this temple building, and thou wilt raise it up in three days?
texts.jhn.2.21: But *he* spoke of the temple of his body.
texts.jhn.2.22: When therefore he was raised from among [the] dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and believed the scripture and the word which Jesus had spoken.
texts.jhn.2.23: And when he was in Jerusalem, at the passover, at the feast, many believed on his name, beholding his signs which he wrought.
texts.jhn.2.24: But Jesus himself did not trust himself to them, because he knew all [men],
texts.jhn.2.25: and that he had not need that any should testify of man, for himself knew what was in man.
texts.jhn.3.1: But there was a man from among the Pharisees, his name Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews;
texts.jhn.3.2: he came to him by night, and said to him, Rabbi, we know that thou art come a teacher from God, for none can do these signs that thou doest unless God be with him.
texts.jhn.3.3: Jesus answered and said to him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except any one be born anew he cannot see the kingdom of God.
texts.jhn.3.4: Nicodemus says to him, How can a man be born being old? can he enter a second time into the womb of his mother and be born?
texts.jhn.3.5: Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except any one be born of water and of Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.jhn.3.6: That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
texts.jhn.3.7: Do not wonder that I said to thee, It is needful that *ye* should be born anew.
texts.jhn.3.8: The wind blows where it will, and thou hearest its voice, but knowest not whence it comes and where it goes: thus is every one that is born of the Spirit.
texts.jhn.3.9: Nicodemus answered and said to him, How can these things be?
texts.jhn.3.10: Jesus answered and said to him, Thou art the teacher of Israel and knowest not these things!
texts.jhn.3.11: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that which we know, and we bear witness of that which we have seen, and ye receive not our witness.
texts.jhn.3.12: If I have said the earthly things to you, and ye believe not, how, if I say the heavenly things to you, will ye believe?
texts.jhn.3.13: And no one has gone up into heaven, save he who came down out of heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven.
texts.jhn.3.14: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, thus must the Son of man be lifted up,
texts.jhn.3.15: that every one who believes on him may [not perish, but] have life eternal.
texts.jhn.3.16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whosoever believes on him may not perish, but have life eternal.
texts.jhn.3.17: For God has not sent his Son into the world that he may judge the world, but that the world may be saved through him.
texts.jhn.3.18: He that believes on him is not judged: but he that believes not has been already judged, because he has not believed on the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
texts.jhn.3.19: And this is the judgment, that light is come into the world, and men have loved darkness rather than light; for their works were evil.
texts.jhn.3.20: For every one that does evil hates the light, and does not come to the light that his works may not be shewn as they are;
texts.jhn.3.21: but he that practises the truth comes to the light, that his works may be manifested that they have been wrought in God.
texts.jhn.3.22: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judaea; and there he abode with them and baptised.
texts.jhn.3.23: And John also was baptising in Aenon, near Salim, because there was a great deal of water there; and they came to [him] and were baptised:
texts.jhn.3.24: for John was not yet cast into prison.
texts.jhn.3.25: There was therefore a reasoning of the disciples of John with a Jew about purification.
texts.jhn.3.26: And they came to John and said to him, Rabbi, he who was with thee beyond the Jordan, to whom thou barest witness, behold, he baptises, and all come to him.
texts.jhn.3.27: John answered and said, A man can receive nothing unless it be given him out of heaven.
texts.jhn.3.28: Ye yourselves bear me witness that I said, I am not the Christ, but, that I am sent before him.
texts.jhn.3.29: He that has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices in heart because of the voice of the bridegroom: this my joy then is fulfilled.
texts.jhn.3.30: He must increase, but I must decrease.
texts.jhn.3.31: He who comes from above is above all. He who has his origin in the earth is of the earth, and speaks [as] of the earth. He who comes out of heaven is above all,
texts.jhn.3.32: [and] what he has seen and has heard, this he testifies; and no one receives his testimony.
texts.jhn.3.33: He that has received his testimony has set to his seal that God is true;
texts.jhn.3.34: for he whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives not the Spirit by measure.
texts.jhn.3.35: The Father loves the Son, and has given all things [to be] in his hand.
texts.jhn.3.36: He that believes on the Son has life eternal, and he that is not subject to the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abides upon him.
texts.jhn.4.1: When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus makes and baptises more disciples than John
texts.jhn.4.2: (however, Jesus himself did not baptise, but his disciples),
texts.jhn.4.3: he left Judaea and went away again unto Galilee.
texts.jhn.4.4: And he must needs pass through Samaria.
texts.jhn.4.5: He comes therefore to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near to the land which Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
texts.jhn.4.6: Now a fountain of Jacob's was there; Jesus therefore, being wearied with the way he had come, sat just as he was at the fountain. It was about the sixth hour.
texts.jhn.4.7: A woman comes out of Samaria to draw water. Jesus says to her, Give me to drink
texts.jhn.4.8: (for his disciples had gone away into the city that they might buy provisions).
texts.jhn.4.9: The Samaritan woman therefore says to him, How dost thou, being a Jew, ask to drink of me who am a Samaritan woman? for Jews have no intercourse with Samaritans.
texts.jhn.4.10: Jesus answered and said to her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that says to thee, Give me to drink, thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
texts.jhn.4.11: The woman says to him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: whence then hast thou the living water?
texts.jhn.4.12: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank of it himself, and his sons, and his cattle?
texts.jhn.4.13: Jesus answered and said to her, Every one who drinks of this water shall thirst again;
texts.jhn.4.14: but whosoever drinks of the water which I shall give him shall never thirst for ever, but the water which I shall give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life.
texts.jhn.4.15: The woman says to him, Sir, give me this water, that I may not thirst nor come here to draw.
texts.jhn.4.16: Jesus says to her, Go, call thy husband, and come here.
texts.jhn.4.17: The woman answered and said, I have not a husband. Jesus says to her, Thou hast well said, I have not a husband;
texts.jhn.4.18: for thou hast had five husbands, and he whom now thou hast is not thy husband: this thou hast spoken truly.
texts.jhn.4.19: The woman says to him, Sir, I see that thou art a prophet.
texts.jhn.4.20: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain, and ye say that in Jerusalem is the place where one must worship.
texts.jhn.4.21: Jesus says to her, Woman, believe me, [the] hour is coming when ye shall neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem worship the Father.
texts.jhn.4.22: Ye worship ye know not what; we worship what we know, for salvation is of the Jews.
texts.jhn.4.23: But [the] hour is coming and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and truth; for also the Father seeks such as his worshippers.
texts.jhn.4.24: God [is] a spirit; and they who worship him must worship [him] in spirit and truth.
texts.jhn.4.25: The woman says to him, I know that Messias is coming, who is called Christ; when *he* comes he will tell us all things.
texts.jhn.4.26: Jesus says to her, I who speak to thee am [he].
texts.jhn.4.27: And upon this came his disciples, and wondered that he spoke with a woman; yet no one said, What seekest thou? or, Why speakest thou with her?
texts.jhn.4.28: The woman then left her waterpot and went away into the city, and says to the men,
texts.jhn.4.29: Come, see a man who told me all things I had ever done: is not he the Christ?
texts.jhn.4.30: They went out of the city and came to him.
texts.jhn.4.31: But meanwhile the disciples asked him saying, Rabbi, eat.
texts.jhn.4.32: But he said to them, I have food to eat which ye do not know.
texts.jhn.4.33: The disciples therefore said to one another, Has any one brought him [anything] to eat?
texts.jhn.4.34: Jesus says to them, My food is that I should do the will of him that has sent me, and that I should finish his work.
texts.jhn.4.35: Do not ye say, that there are yet four months and the harvest comes? Behold, I say to you, Lift up your eyes and behold the fields, for they are already white to harvest.
texts.jhn.4.36: He that reaps receives wages and gathers fruit unto life eternal, that both he that sows and he that reaps may rejoice together.
texts.jhn.4.37: For in this is [verified] the true saying, It is one who sows and another who reaps.
texts.jhn.4.38: I have sent you to reap that on which ye have not laboured; others have laboured, and ye have entered into their labours.
texts.jhn.4.39: But many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him because of the word of the woman who bore witness, He told me all things that I had ever done.
texts.jhn.4.40: When therefore the Samaritans came to him they asked him to abide with them, and he abode there two days.
texts.jhn.4.41: And more a great deal believed on account of his word;
texts.jhn.4.42: and they said to the woman, [It is] no longer on account of thy saying that we believe, for we have heard him ourselves, and we know that this is indeed the Saviour of the world.
texts.jhn.4.43: But after the two days he went forth thence and went away into Galilee,
texts.jhn.4.44: for Jesus himself bore witness that a prophet has no honour in his own country.
texts.jhn.4.45: When therefore he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all that he had done in Jerusalem during the feast, for they also went to the feast.
texts.jhn.4.46: He came therefore again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain courtier in Capernaum whose son was sick.
texts.jhn.4.47: He, having heard that Jesus had come out of Judaea into Galilee, went to him and asked [him] that he would come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
texts.jhn.4.48: Jesus therefore said to him, Unless ye see signs and wonders ye will not believe.
texts.jhn.4.49: The courtier says to him, Sir, come down ere my child die.
texts.jhn.4.50: Jesus says to him, Go, thy son lives. And the man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and went his way.
texts.jhn.4.51: But already, as he was going down, his servants met him and brought [him] word saying, Thy child lives.
texts.jhn.4.52: He inquired therefore from them the hour at which he got better. And they said to him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
texts.jhn.4.53: The father therefore knew that [it was] in that hour in which Jesus said to him, Thy son lives; and he believed, himself and his whole house.
texts.jhn.4.54: This second sign again did Jesus, being come out of Judaea into Galilee.
texts.jhn.5.1: After these things was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
texts.jhn.5.2: Now there is in Jerusalem, at the sheepgate, a pool, which is called in Hebrew, Bethesda, having five porches.
texts.jhn.5.3: In these lay a multitude of sick, blind, lame, withered, [awaiting the moving of the water.
texts.jhn.5.4: For an angel descended at a certain season in the pool and troubled the water. Whoever therefore first went in after the troubling of the water became well, whatever disease he laboured under.]
texts.jhn.5.5: But there was a certain man there who had been suffering under his infirmity thirty and eight years.
texts.jhn.5.6: Jesus seeing this [man] lying [there], and knowing that he was [in that state] now a great length of time, says to him, Wouldest thou become well?
texts.jhn.5.7: The infirm [man] answered him, Sir, I have not a man, in order, when the water has been troubled, to cast me into the pool; but while I am coming another descends before me.
texts.jhn.5.8: Jesus says to him, Arise, take up thy couch and walk.
texts.jhn.5.9: And immediately the man became well, and took up his couch and walked: and on that day was sabbath.
texts.jhn.5.10: The Jews therefore said to the healed [man], It is sabbath, it is not permitted thee to take up thy couch.
texts.jhn.5.11: He answered them, He that made me well, *he* said to me, Take up thy couch and walk.
texts.jhn.5.12: They asked him [therefore], Who is the man who said to thee, Take up thy couch and walk?
texts.jhn.5.13: But he that had been healed knew not who it was, for Jesus had slidden away, there being a crowd in the place.
texts.jhn.5.14: After these things Jesus finds him in the temple, and said to him, Behold, thou art become well: sin no more, that something worse do not happen to thee.
texts.jhn.5.15: The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
texts.jhn.5.16: And for this the Jews persecuted Jesus [and sought to kill him], because he had done these things on sabbath.
texts.jhn.5.17: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto and I work.
texts.jhn.5.18: For this therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he had not only violated the sabbath, but also said that God was his own Father, making himself equal with God.
texts.jhn.5.19: Jesus therefore answered and said to them, Verily, verily, I say to you, The Son can do nothing of himself save whatever he sees the Father doing: for whatever things *he* does, these things also the Son does in like manner.
texts.jhn.5.20: For the Father loves the Son and shews him all things which he himself does; and he will shew him greater works than these, that ye may wonder.
texts.jhn.5.21: For even as the Father raises the dead and quickens [them], thus the Son also quickens whom he will:
texts.jhn.5.22: for neither does the Father judge any one, but has given all judgment to the Son;
texts.jhn.5.23: that all may honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He who honours not the Son, honours not the Father who has sent him.
texts.jhn.5.24: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that he that hears my word, and believes him that has sent me, has life eternal, and does not come into judgment, but is passed out of death into life.
texts.jhn.5.25: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that an hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and they that have heard shall live.
texts.jhn.5.26: For even as the Father has life in himself, so he has given to the Son also to have life in himself,
texts.jhn.5.27: and has given him authority to execute judgment [also], because he is Son of man.
texts.jhn.5.28: Wonder not at this, for an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs shall hear his voice,
texts.jhn.5.29: and shall go forth; those that have practised good, to resurrection of life, and those that have done evil, to resurrection of judgment.
texts.jhn.5.30: I cannot do anything of myself; as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is righteous, because I do not seek my will, but the will of him that has sent me.
texts.jhn.5.31: If I bear witness concerning myself, my witness is not true.
texts.jhn.5.32: It is another who bears witness concerning me, and I know that the witness which he bears concerning me is true.
texts.jhn.5.33: Ye have sent unto John, and he has borne witness to the truth.
texts.jhn.5.34: But I do not receive witness from man, but I say this that *ye* might be saved.
texts.jhn.5.35: *He* was the burning and shining lamp, and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light.
texts.jhn.5.36: But I have the witness [that is] greater than [that] of John; for the works which the Father has given me that I should complete them, the works themselves which I do, bear witness concerning me that the Father has sent me.
texts.jhn.5.37: And the Father who has sent me himself has borne witness concerning me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor have seen his shape,
texts.jhn.5.38: and ye have not his word abiding in you; for whom *he* hath sent, him ye do not believe.
texts.jhn.5.39: Ye search the scriptures, for ye think that in them ye have life eternal, and they it is which bear witness concerning me;
texts.jhn.5.40: and ye will not come to me that ye might have life.
texts.jhn.5.41: I do not receive glory from men,
texts.jhn.5.42: but I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.
texts.jhn.5.43: I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not; if another come in his own name, him ye will receive.
texts.jhn.5.44: How can ye believe, who receive glory one of another, and seek not the glory which [comes] from God alone?
texts.jhn.5.45: Think not that I will accuse you to the Father: there is [one] who accuses you, Moses, on whom ye trust;
texts.jhn.5.46: for if ye had believed Moses, ye would have believed me, for he wrote of me.
texts.jhn.5.47: But if ye do not believe his writings, how shall ye believe my words?
texts.jhn.6.1: After these things Jesus went away beyond the sea of Galilee, [or] of Tiberias,
texts.jhn.6.2: and a great crowd followed him, because they saw the signs which he wrought upon the sick.
texts.jhn.6.3: And Jesus went up into the mountain, and there sat with his disciples:
texts.jhn.6.4: but the passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
texts.jhn.6.5: Jesus then, lifting up his eyes and seeing that a great crowd is coming to him, says to Philip, Whence shall we buy loaves that these may eat?
texts.jhn.6.6: But this he said trying him, for he knew what he was going to do.
texts.jhn.6.7: Philip answered him, Loaves for two hundred denarii are not sufficient for them, that each may have some little [portion].
texts.jhn.6.8: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says to him,
texts.jhn.6.9: There is a little boy here who has five barley loaves and two small fishes; but this, what is it for so many?
texts.jhn.6.10: [And] Jesus said, Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place: the men therefore sat down, in number about five thousand.
texts.jhn.6.11: And Jesus took the loaves, and having given thanks, distributed [them] to those that were set down; and in like manner of the small fishes as much as they would.
texts.jhn.6.12: And when they had been filled, he says to his disciples, Gather together the fragments which are over and above, that nothing may be lost.
texts.jhn.6.13: They gathered [them] therefore together, and filled twelve hand-baskets full of fragments of the five barley loaves, which were over and above to those that had eaten.
texts.jhn.6.14: The men therefore, having seen the sign which Jesus had done, said, This is truly the prophet which is coming into the world.
texts.jhn.6.15: Jesus therefore knowing that they were going to come and seize him, that they might make [him] king, departed again to the mountain himself alone.
texts.jhn.6.16: But when evening was come, his disciples went down to the sea,
texts.jhn.6.17: and having gone on board ship, they went over the sea to Capernaum. And it had already become dark, and Jesus had not come to them,
texts.jhn.6.18: and the sea was agitated by a strong wind blowing.
texts.jhn.6.19: Having rowed then about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they see Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the ship; and they were frightened.
texts.jhn.6.20: But he says to them, It is I: be not afraid.
texts.jhn.6.21: They were willing therefore to receive him into the ship; and immediately the ship was at the land to which they went.
texts.jhn.6.22: On the morrow the crowd which stood on the other side of the sea, having seen that there was no other little ship there except that into which his disciples had got, and that Jesus had not gone with his disciples into the ship, but [that] his disciples had gone away alone;
texts.jhn.6.23: (but other little ships out of Tiberias came near to the place where they ate bread after the Lord had given thanks;)
texts.jhn.6.24: when therefore the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, *they* got into the ships, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
texts.jhn.6.25: And having found him the other side of the sea, they said to him, Rabbi, when art thou arrived here?
texts.jhn.6.26: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say to you, Ye seek me not because ye have seen signs, but because ye have eaten of the loaves and been filled.
texts.jhn.6.27: Work not [for] the food which perishes, but [for] the food which abides unto life eternal, which the Son of man shall give to you; for him has the Father sealed, [even] God.
texts.jhn.6.28: They said therefore to him, What should we do that we may work the works of God?
texts.jhn.6.29: Jesus answered and said to them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom *he* has sent.
texts.jhn.6.30: They said therefore to him, What sign then doest thou that we may see and believe thee? what dost thou work?
texts.jhn.6.31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.
texts.jhn.6.32: Jesus therefore said to them, Verily, verily, I say to you, [It is] not Moses that has given you the bread out of heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.
texts.jhn.6.33: For the bread of God is he who comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.
texts.jhn.6.34: They said therefore to him, Lord, ever give to us this bread.
texts.jhn.6.35: [And] Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life: he that comes to me shall never hunger, and he that believes on me shall never thirst at any time.
texts.jhn.6.36: But I have said to you, that ye have also seen me and do not believe.
texts.jhn.6.37: All that the Father gives me shall come to me, and him that comes to me I will not at all cast out.
texts.jhn.6.38: For I am come down from heaven, not that I should do *my* will, but the will of him that has sent me.
texts.jhn.6.39: And this is the will of him that has sent me, that of all that he has given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up in the last day.
texts.jhn.6.40: For this is the will of my Father, that every one who sees the Son, and believes on him, should have life eternal; and I will raise him up at the last day.
texts.jhn.6.41: The Jews therefore murmured about him, because he said, I am the bread which has come down out of heaven.
texts.jhn.6.42: And they said, Is not this Jesus the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we have known? how then does *he* say, I am come down out of heaven?
texts.jhn.6.43: Jesus therefore answered and said to them, Murmur not among yourselves.
texts.jhn.6.44: No one can come to me except the Father who has sent me draw him, and I will raise him up in the last day.
texts.jhn.6.45: It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every one that has heard from the Father [himself], and has learned [of him], comes to me;
texts.jhn.6.46: not that any one has seen the Father, except he who is of God, he has seen the Father.
texts.jhn.6.47: Verily, verily, I say to you, He that believes [on me] has life eternal.
texts.jhn.6.48: I am the bread of life.
texts.jhn.6.49: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
texts.jhn.6.50: This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that one may eat of it and not die.
texts.jhn.6.51: I am the living bread which has come down out of heaven: if any one shall have eaten of this bread he shall live for ever; but the bread withal which I shall give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
texts.jhn.6.52: The Jews therefore contended among themselves, saying, How can he give us this flesh to eat?
texts.jhn.6.53: Jesus therefore said to them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Unless ye shall have eaten the flesh of the Son of man, and drunk his blood, ye have no life in yourselves.
texts.jhn.6.54: He that eats my flesh and drinks my blood has life eternal, and I will raise him up at the last day:
texts.jhn.6.55: for my flesh is truly food and my blood is truly drink.
texts.jhn.6.56: He that eats my flesh and drinks my blood dwells in me and I in him.
texts.jhn.6.57: As the living Father has sent me and I live on account of the Father, *he* also who eats me shall live also on account of me.
texts.jhn.6.58: This is the bread which has come down out of heaven. Not as the fathers ate and died: he that eats this bread shall live for ever.
texts.jhn.6.59: These things he said in [the] synagogue, teaching in Capernaum.
texts.jhn.6.60: Many therefore of his disciples having heard [it] said, This word is hard; who can hear it?
texts.jhn.6.61: But Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples murmur concerning this, said to them, Does this offend you?
texts.jhn.6.62: If then ye see the Son of man ascending up where he was before?
texts.jhn.6.63: It is the Spirit which quickens, the flesh profits nothing: the words which I have spoken unto you are spirit and are life.
texts.jhn.6.64: But there are some of you who do not believe. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would deliver him up.
texts.jhn.6.65: And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no one can come to me unless it be given to him from the Father.
texts.jhn.6.66: From that [time] many of his disciples went away back and walked no more with him.
texts.jhn.6.67: Jesus therefore said to the twelve, Will ye also go away?
texts.jhn.6.68: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast words of life eternal;
texts.jhn.6.69: and we have believed and known that thou art the holy one of God.
texts.jhn.6.70: Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you the twelve? and of you one is a devil.
texts.jhn.6.71: Now he spoke of Judas [the son] of Simon, Iscariote, for he [it was who] should deliver him up, being one of the twelve.
texts.jhn.7.1: And after these things Jesus walked in Galilee, for he would not walk in Judaea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
texts.jhn.7.2: Now the tabernacles, the feast of the Jews, was near.
texts.jhn.7.3: His brethren therefore said to him, Remove hence and go into Judaea, that thy disciples also may see thy works which thou doest;
texts.jhn.7.4: for no one does anything in secret and himself seeks to be [known] in public. If thou doest these things, manifest thyself to the world:
texts.jhn.7.5: for neither did his brethren believe on him.
texts.jhn.7.6: Jesus therefore says to them, My time is not yet come, but your time is always ready.
texts.jhn.7.7: The world cannot hate you, but me it hates, because I bear witness concerning it that its works are evil.
texts.jhn.7.8: Ye, go ye up to this feast. I go not up to this feast, for *my* time is not yet fulfilled.
texts.jhn.7.9: Having said these things to them he abode in Galilee.
texts.jhn.7.10: But when his brethren had gone up, then he himself also went up to the feast, not openly, but as in secret.
texts.jhn.7.11: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?
texts.jhn.7.12: And there was much murmuring concerning him among the crowds. Some said, He is [a] good [man]; others said, No; but he deceives the crowd.
texts.jhn.7.13: However, no one spoke openly concerning him on account of [their] fear of the Jews.
texts.jhn.7.14: But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
texts.jhn.7.15: The Jews therefore wondered, saying, How knows this [man] letters, having never learned?
texts.jhn.7.16: Jesus therefore answered them and said, My doctrine is not mine, but [that] of him that has sent me.
texts.jhn.7.17: If any one desire to practise his will, he shall know concerning the doctrine, whether it is of God, or [that] I speak from myself.
texts.jhn.7.18: He that speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but he that seeks the glory of him that has sent him, he is true, and unrighteousness is not in him.
texts.jhn.7.19: Has not Moses given you the law, and no one of you practises the law? Why do ye seek to kill me?
texts.jhn.7.20: The crowd answered [and said], Thou hast a demon: who seeks to kill thee?
texts.jhn.7.21: Jesus answered and said to them, I have done one work, and ye all wonder.
texts.jhn.7.22: Therefore Moses gave you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and ye circumcise a man on sabbath.
texts.jhn.7.23: If a man receives circumcision on sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be violated, are ye angry with me because I have made a man entirely sound on sabbath?
texts.jhn.7.24: Judge not according to sight, but judge righteous judgment.
texts.jhn.7.25: Some therefore of those of Jerusalem said, Is not this he whom they seek to kill?
texts.jhn.7.26: and behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Have the rulers then indeed recognised that this is the Christ?
texts.jhn.7.27: But [as to] this [man] we know whence he is. Now [as to] the Christ, when he comes, no one knows whence he is.
texts.jhn.7.28: Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, Ye both know me and ye know whence I am; and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye do not know.
texts.jhn.7.29: I know him, because I am from him, and *he* has sent me.
texts.jhn.7.30: They sought therefore to take him; and no one laid his hand upon him, because his hour had not yet come.
texts.jhn.7.31: But many of the crowd believed on him, and said, Will the Christ, when he comes, do more signs than those which this [man] has done?
texts.jhn.7.32: The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things concerning him, and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers that they might take him.
texts.jhn.7.33: Jesus therefore said, Yet a little while I am with you, and I go to him that has sent me.
texts.jhn.7.34: Ye shall seek me and shall not find [me], and where I am ye cannot come.
texts.jhn.7.35: The Jews therefore said to one another, Where is he about to go that we shall not find him? Is he about to go to the dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
texts.jhn.7.36: What word is this which he said, Ye shall seek me and shall not find [me]; and where I am ye cannot come?
texts.jhn.7.37: In the last, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried saying, If any one thirst, let him come to me and drink.
texts.jhn.7.38: He that believes on me, as the scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.
texts.jhn.7.39: But this he said concerning the Spirit, which they that believed on him were about to receive; for [the] Spirit was not yet, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
